analysis.name: Alexander Francis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was awful.  He is unhelpful as well as a terrible test maker.  His class ended up with a giant unspoken curve at the end so he could adjust the grades due to us all doing so poorly.  If you have to take this class good luck.  And his acoustics class is worse if anything.

It is obvious the professor knows what he is talking about. He is incredibly knowledgeable in linguistics; however, he does not frequently lecture about things relevant to what is being tested. The TAs are the only reason anyone knows what to do. He can be an excellent resource but does not help much during lecture.

The class was challenging but I felt like he was very understanding and worked with the class. He adjusted his grading when we were all doing bad. There are some topics that are hard but I think his lectures plus the textbook explained them pretty well. I really enjoyed this class and Dr. Francis is an interesting guy. Talk to him outside of class!
The homework and quizzes are unrelated to what you're working on in class, prof gets off topic everyday and is unwilling to meet with students when needed.

Dr. Francis made this class way harder than it had to be. I feel like I know absolutely nothing about phonetics. I do not feel prepared for grad school. He even admits Praat is not going to be significant for us in our careers, but the whole class revolves around Praat. It's awful. Take with someone else if you can.

analysis.name: Andres Vargas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He 's very helpful in class and at office hours. You do not need a textbook if you attend lectures and use slides. You should probably practice his problem sets a lot, I didn't realize this till the final, so don't be like me. Hotseat points boost grades ideally by a letter grade and his exams are pretty difficult since there are no sample exams.

Take his class, seriously! A good professor, very helpful !!!!!! His lectures and slides are easy to understand and helpful enough. No need to buy the textbook. And also, he took participation points. Exams are moderate, and getting A's for exams is not that hard. It's all multiple choice questions. If you do all the homework, it's A in your hand!

Vargas is an incredible professor. In addition to teaching very well, he uses third-party elements (e.g., news clips) to enhance his lectures. The class is not difficult; he gives extra credit for merely showing up to class (very generous), and the hw/practices exams are exactly like the exams  very approachable guy & knowledgeable.

Dr Vargas is one of the greatest economics professors and lectures I've had! he is super kind and very helpful. His lectures are well organized with lots of examples and always willing to answer questions before, during, and after class. I've had him for macro too and although the topics can be quiet hard he can help you through understanding well!

This was an ok professor, but his lectures are basically him reading presentations. He doesn't make content easy, and I would learn the same amount of things through the textbook or youtube. He says attendance isn't mandatory, but uses iClicker for points. Not the best if you want to be genuinely engaged during lectures.

analysis.name: Andrew Toms
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Only thing that could make him better would be if he was right handed
Wore a pickachu hat to lecture once you could say he's a pretty cool guy. Most of the time his lectures on last about 20 minutes.

Toms is a pretty funny/entertaining guy.  He always throws in some jokes or goes on a funny rant during lectures.  He also writes the exams to be very easy.  His teaching skills are just average in my opinion.  He uses the same examples in lecture that are used in the textbook and tends not to fully explain the key concepts.

Doesn't waste any time. Gives you exactly what you need for exams. He wasn't even my prof and I went to all his lectures anyway outside of the first week. He's also hilarious in a kind of out of pocket way, which is awesome.

Solid lecturer, but can go too fast at times and the class information is tough. Something this professor could do better is repeating important information. Stories were funny, and made the lectures better.

analysis.name: Andrei Gabrielov
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gabrielov's like that sweet old grandad you have. The kind tries to teach you things but in the end you don't really know what he's saying and end up smiling and nodding at everything. Now imagine that grandad being Russian. Needless to say, I didn't understand much of what he said and just like at family dinners, I excused myself and left.

Basically the wacky uncle of the Math department. He seems like a very friendly person, but he skips steps in example problems, is very difficult to understand (thick accent), and doesn't explain new material very well. He may also be a Soviet sleeper cell, but that's based more on suspicion than evidence.

As lecturer, Gabrielov does not excel. He has a moderately thick russian accent, and when combined with a small amount of background noise and a low quality microphone he can be hard to understand in lecture halls.  His strengths lie in face to face interactions. He is extremely intelligent and resolve any issues you have with course material.

Absolutely terrible. So hard to understand, skips steps all the time, and writes really hard tests. Going to class with Gabrielov isn't even worth it. I survived through using the internet, but it was not a good experience. Avoid taking at all costs.

His handwriting is very bad, he reuses paper so you can see work on the other side, his accent is difficult at times, his lectures have NO structure whatsoever and he blames students for his own mistakes and says 'you need to watch what I'm doing and tell me if I make a mistake'. If you get him, watch other lectures on BoilerCast. Good luck...

analysis.name: Adrian Wolanski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My GOAT. Professor Wolanski was amazing. I actually did better here than in MGMT 30301 (which is basically AP Stats). He's very available in office hours, quick with emails, funny, and genuinely cares about Purdue (he's from Indiana). His engaging style encourages collaboration and discussion, so you're basically studying while learning.

Got an A in this class and a C in 30301. The content in this class was harder, but Wolanski makes it easier to understand. He is very caring and really wants you to do good. Go to his office hours and get help on homework it makes the class a lot easier. Do not wait to do the homework last minute it takes a lot of time. He is an amazing professor!

He is such an amazing prof. He really cares about every single student he has. He makes sure that he know everyone's name and gets to know them. I would say go to office hours because homework can be challenging. Another piece of advice I would give is to make sure you to to lecture because he goes over everything that you need to know.

He knows what he is doing, and he tries his best to make it as easy as it can be while not simplifying too much. Homework takes a while, but they're just once weekly. Exams are OK, 15 multiple choice questions don't sound bad, but you have to know the material, just like every other class. Not a class to stress about, which I liked.

I hate stats so I dreaded this class but Prof Wolanski made up for it. He is very into what he teaches and wants to see his students succeed. He knows that this class is a pathway course for a lot of classes and thats the only reason students take it so he tries to make everything as painless as possible.

analysis.name: Andrew Freed
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 292 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Honestly my favorite professor at Purdue. He is always so excited about what he teaches and goes through so much effort to show us cool examples. I love how you can ask him questions about anything EAPS related on Hotseat. I have learned and enjoyed this class so much because of him.
This guy is awesome. He keeps class interesting and tells you what is exactly on each exam. If every teacher was like him I would gladly go to class everyday!

I loved taking this class - it was such a nice break from my other ones . Attendance isn't mandatory, but he does give in class participation quizzes  a lot. There isn't really any reason not to go to lecture, anyway - he makes it very entertaining. Don't bother buying the textbook - all the homework questions can be googled.
Easy A class, and enough extra credit, many announcement and email to remind you to remember the deadline. Patience!

Freed is awesome and hilarious. Makes really nerdy jokes a lot. We just watch a ton of movies and he makes the lectures interesting. Exams are pretty clear cut and he goes over everything on the test. He's also super nice, even to give us an alternate exam date early in the week before break, so we don't have to wait around on campus.

analysis.name: Cari Ann Boersma
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Boersma is awesome. She makes an effort to foster a community in the class. You will become a much better speaker by the end of the class. As long as you participate and put effort into the assignments, you will do well. One of the most fun classes I've taken at this school.
She gave good feedback on my assignments and understood us as students. Also was very welcoming and everyone in my class liked her.

She made this class so fun by fostering a very nice community within the class. It was my favorite one this semester! Very presentation based, and you become way more comfortable presenting in front of the class by the end with feedback from her and your classmates. Just follow her instructions, and you'll be all set.

She is a very good COM teacher. She makes everything that we learn very relatable. The class focuses more on presentations with feedback from your peers. The class is pretty laid-back as long as you do what is required of you. She makes the class very fun!

Cari runs an easy yet fair class. as long as you do the quizzes and prepare a little for presentation you can get a A. The class atmosphere is lively, and I looked forward to going to class every day.

analysis.name: Andy Hudmon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: lectures are very easy to understand. you will leave lecture feeling like you understand what is going on instead of studying for hours trying to figure out what the bullet points are saying. very concise and engaging

Dr. Hudmon is the one redeemable factor in this mess of a class. He works hard to make sure we are understanding his material, which can be difficult at times. However, his exams are extremely fair in comparison to Krusemark's and he pulls directly from the slides. Exam review sessions are helpful, given he actually answers questions unlike others.

Hudmon seems to really care about his students and explains lecture in way for us to understand. His exam questions come straight from the slides or iClicker questions. He emphasized important information that we needed to know (like for homework or exams). He rarely fell behind in slides and if he ever did, he made extra videos to compensate.

Dr. Hudmon is the only reason this class is bearable. His lectures are much easier to follow and he takes time to ensure we are understanding the material. Exam content is pulled straight from the slides and he will even recycle past exam questions. If he was the course coordinator rather than Krusemark, student performance would be way better.

Dr. Hudmon is SO much better than Dr. Krusemark. Don't be discouraged by the horror that is exam one, once you reach Hudmon's content things become a lot more clear. Dr. Hudmon is extremely knowledgeable and seems to care a lot more about his impact on students, he will tell you the key takeaways you need to know for the exams and future courses.

analysis.name: Konstantinos Ameranis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ameranis is goated! I found value in his lectures, and his style of teaching is very open and flexible. The accent was a bit hard to understand at times, but otherwise no complaints. Exams were tricky, but nicely curved. Do get started early on the projects tho. Also, his lectures on graphs & hashing were some of the best ive ever seen

Professor Ameranis speaks clearly. Even though he is "new" at teaching, he gets to the point in lectures, he is not monotone or repetitive which makes the 50 minute lectures a breeze. If you have never programmed in your life, well lets just say you will need to put in a lot more effort than those kids who have been programming since 6th grade.

He's a new professor, but by no means unexperienced. I really enjoyed the setup of the lectures, as the concepts explained in class clicked very quickly apposed to if I had to miss a class and learn the information outside of class. 

Main thing: If you show up to classes, put in effort in class, and think critically you will do well.

He was a great professor even though it was his first time teaching the class. His lectures are engaging and he will ask the class questions throughout lecture. He is very accessible at his office hours and he was always very helpful at answering questions.

analysis.name: Bushra Ferdousi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Project instructions were consistently vague, and the final project was graded unfairly. Feedback was returned too late to incorporate, yet most of the class received unnecessarily low grades. Points were deducted for not being “creative” despite using queries taught in class. TA guidance also conflicted with grading.

Poorly organized, hard to follow. She had 1 assginment in Excel and 2 in Tableau. The course is a TABLEAU class, there shouldn't be Excel assignments! Spacing between due dates was bad. GRILLED project presentation groups in front of all students. Her grading was inconsistent, there was hidden grading criteria which many people got points off for.
Incredibly difficult to understand and grades unfairly. Uncooperative with students and refuses to help push students in the right direction.
She does not know how to teach, consistent issues and wrong queries/data taught.
professor is not good at explaining things in the lecture and isnt very engaging

analysis.name: Becky Bokrand
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She gives amazing bullet points on what to study for exams. The lectures are super boring, but that is more so accounting than her. Dr. Bokrand is super kind and passionate about what she does. She gives great resources to succeed, and extra credit here and there. The class is an easy GPA booster, even if you have trouble staying awake.

Dr. Bokrand was a great professor and a lecturer who wasn't boring to listen to for the 50-minute class time. There were reviews and homework for each chapter learned, and there are 3 total exams (including the final). The exams are difficult if you don't understand the material.

I personally didnt find the class very interesting, but Dr. Bokrand was very passionate and knowledgeable about the topic. Additionally, she was very nice about extra credit, which really helps your grade as the exams are not easy. This class is straight forward, but you need to put in the effort to see the results.

I took Dr. Bokrand's accounting class and thought she was a good professor. Some material was confusing at first, but her explanations and review days helped a lot. Homework was challenging but useful, and exams reflected what she reviewed.

Great professor, the notes style is not the most useful. Provided is fill in the blank notes. I believe handwriting them is better. Be sure to use the book and the practice provided for exam prep. Otherwise, a memorization heavy class.

analysis.name: George Adams
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 143 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His test's do not test you over what you have learned or studied for. The material is fairly easy, so he likes to word the questions so they are all impossible to read or comprehend.

By far the most overrated professor at Purdue. Don't understand why so many people like him. Only his delivery is good, his content and exams suck. He doesn't slow down at all and his lectures are quite frankly hard to understand. He assumes that everyone is as passionate as him and thinks everyone understands hardware the same way he does.
His slides is full of information and exams are not related to what was covered in class.

Really passionate about what he teaches, but because of his EE background, he goes way too in-depth on topics and rambles a lot during class. Exams are extremely hard even if you study and class has over 1000 slides for the final exam.  Too much material crammed into one course imo which makes retaining knowledge on what was taught difficult.

While Prof. Adams is clearly passionate about what he teaches and is a generally good lecturer, he has by far some of the WORST tests I have ever seen. Focuses on testing whether you remember obscure trivia rather than if you truly understand the material. Furthermore, the tests are structured to be ambiguous and an english comprehension test.

analysis.name: Bettina Klose
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor isn't just a "tough grader". ECON 340 is essentially a math class, but you can complete all of your math perfectly and receive a C if your work can't "teach another student how to do the work as well". You're supposed to write a textbook for every assignment, and feedback is vague or nonexistent. TAs were bad, too. Avoid if you can.

I had Dr.Klose for Game Theory (ECON 451) and she was fine. I was worried with the bad reviews, but most of the content was not hard to follow. Guessing that most of the reviews are from an earlier period. The exams were difficult, but we were told what to study. This course was more difficult than most but not the hardest I have ever taken.

Poorly designed course. She lets the curve do all the work. You will pass the class as long as you aren't the very bottom. Her grading is the most unreasonable and inconsistent I've ever seen out of all my years of undergrad, graduate and even high school. This is the first and only time I've cried because of class. Avoid at all costs if possible.

Bad lectures, I would ask for help with something, and she seemingly wouldn't read the full question before responding with a nonhelpful answer. Prepare to teach yourself. I repeatedly had to go and protest against her grading mistakes she made in grading to give me my correct score. I should not have to review the professors grading ever.

Dr. Klose is lecture-heavy. Her entire class is composed of going over material in a pretty bland way. She's unclear on how much work to show during problem sets and exams. Exams are pretty tight on time.

analysis.name: Josh Boyd
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: COM 204 is a challenging course, but really, if you go to class, follow the rubric and his grading scale closely, and consult Dr. Boyd and his TA's for help, you will succeed. Dr. Boyd is honest in his grading and his words, and wants his students to grow; however, a level of commitment and consistency is expected for this class.

While the class was okay I found myself losing some sanity over it. Every assignment is graded out of five. While the rubric is clear, it is very objective and opinion based. Major papers are graded on the five-point scale and then multiplied by 6 to get your grade out of 30. Same for the exams. DO NOT use Grammarly; he considers it AI.

This class was difficult, but if you put in genuine effort you can get a good grade! Go to office hours on both major papers! I got a poor grade on the first paper, but still managed to get an A in the class, so don't give up. Don't ever skip lectures, no excuses. He does not post anything online! This being said, his class will teach you a lot.

This class is ridiculously nitpicky. I understand the need to teach students the importance of clarity when it comes to writing, but the way each assignment is graded makes it nearly impossible to succeed. Every assignment is graded out of 5 and, oftentimes, the grading is subjective under the guise of an objective, "clear rubric".
Incredibly tough grader. He uses a 5-point scale for grading and if you meet all requirements on the rubric, you get a 3. Good luck, it's rough.

analysis.name: Craig Brown
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The rest of the reviews are very telling for Professor Brown. I am suprised Purdue admin hasnt seen this and looked into his teaching style. Basically, he teaches by going at 2x speed through things he expects that you know to teach complex topics. He does not blend the theory and math very well together and makes things very difficult. dont. take.

lectures are very confusing and hard to follow and do not aid you properly for the exams that he writes.  I genuinely feel like I understood the content when studying for an exam but would give questions on the exam that are nothing to do with what we learned. Brightspace page has no information. Cold calls sometimes and is rude and unapproachable

Professor Brown is extremely disorganized. He puts material on exams that we never learned, and the study guides are useless. No answer keys are posted, and lectures aren't tied to textbook chapters. Homework isn't reopened, so there's no way to review or improve. You'll end up teaching yourself everything just to keep up. Would not recommend.

One of the less enjoyable courses I've taken at Purdue. He does not seem to be trying to help when asked, as previous review mentioned, refuses to show clear grading standard, refuses to give homework and test answers, practice paper is pretty much irrelevant from actual test. Allows cheat sheet, has a take home final that is in the form of essay.
Craig is literally a king. Exams are def hard though. Zoom class on Fridays which was a plus. Can see why people may find him intimidating but he's actually super nice.

analysis.name: Beatriz Galarza Tohen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the most caring profs I've had at Purdue. I remember near the end of the semester she told me that my smile genuinely brightened her day. Said at the beginning of the semester that she would always take our side no matter what. Genuine unconditional kindness that you don't see often elsewhere (but should).

ENGR 131 isn't a hard class. It's not too exciting either, but Prof. Galarza did her best to make classes kinda fun or have us practice an engineering soft skill (teamwork). 
Prof. Galarza is one of the nicest, most caring professors at Purdue. She also bumped my A- up to an A because I asked (the FYE 3.2 GPA, iykyk), because I got to know her.

She might be one of the most caring professors at this university. She's always available for her students and she truly wants you to succeed. ENGR 131 wasn't a hard class but I had a 7:30, and I'm really thankful that I had her class because I didn't often dread getting up to go to it. She also gives you a lot of studio time to work on projects.

ENGR 13100 I think is a pretty tedious class because the course fits a lot into a few months. Dr. Galarza made the class so much more tolerable. She is a sweet and supportive teacher and is the first person at Purdue who made me feel like I belonged. She makes effort to know all of her students personally and really cares about their well-being.

Professor Galarza is super caring and always makes sure to asks students how they are doing. She is also very helpful when answering students' questions. The class curriculum itself is slow and tedious though so I would recommend taking ENGR 133 over ENGR 131 if you're taking a lighter course load.

analysis.name: Bruno Ribeiro
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst ever. The slides are not well organized and have many mistakes. The homeworks are peculiar and just wasting of time.
He is not a good teacher. English is bad and nonlogical
He is trying to persuade us that he is a good teacher and beg us to connect with him at office hour. But, you are unable to convey us the information that you can solve the issue at class.

Riberio is what happens when a circus clown is asked to teach a 300-level CS course. Horrendous slides have no takeaway material to help you with the homework or exams. No communication with the TAs. Will humbly brag how he asked android to change its facial recognition code several times in the semester. Maybe I should write that on the final.

I don't know what to say. He is passionate and his English is fluent. But his logic is sooo bad that it could make you feel like: what is he doing for the whole class and why am I here. Also, he made too many political jokes and lauged at the joke made by himself, which would be really awkward for international students.

analysis.name: Casey Krusemark
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Krusemark has to be the worst professor out the pre-pharmacy curriculum. He could never give straightforward answers during exam review sessions and wouldn't know the answers to his own questions. Slideshows are an absolute eye sore and information dump, and somehow everything is important given how hyperspecific and hard his exams are.

If you value your sanity, please take this godforsaken class anywhere else. "Unlike most sports games, you can all win this class!" (quoted directly from his first day analogies), and then proceeds to have exam averages in the low fifties. I am a victim of this man's poor ability to teach and will have nightmares about his exams.

biochem is supposed to be a challenging course, but  not like this. his section of the course makes no sense, and he agrees bc he confuses himself and cant even answer questions from students. he seems like a nice guy, but as a professor... he is terrible. his counterpart in this course may be the only reason why students pass.

It's wild to think he's the course coordinator when he is the reason students don't pass this class. For a course coordinator, he says a lot of "I think" and "maybe"s like he doesn't know what he's talking about (which is true, he doesn't). He's also the type to start the semester with a speech about how everyone can get As and why he won't curve

This class is a joke. Most of your grade will come from how you score on the exams, but there are very few resources to help you succeed, even if you go to all of the lectures and pay attention. Dr. Krusemark is extremely vague about the content breakdown on the exams and refuses to provide answer keys for the practice exams.

analysis.name: Congfang Huang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Classes are monotonous and poorly prepared. The slides are often confusing and overtly abstract for rather simple topics. And, at times, it's very difficult to understand the professor's explanations. Grading is generous, but her teaching style is not. Would not take this class with this professor again.

Congfang genuinely cares about her students, especially when you are willing to discuss with her. However, I DO think Congfang needs a better preparation of the course, especially for teaching students materials in a logical and mutually understandable way. You might have to rely mostly on yourself for the course, although the grading is generous.

Congfang's IE 230 class is made up almost entirely of exam credit. There is barely any material to actively practice the topics covered in lecture. She is very hard to understand, which I know is not a fair criticism but it should still be taken into account. Her slides are just mindless info dumps with little to no analysis of the topics.

Grading Scale is pretty lenient, with an 84 being the minimum grade for an A. Not a lot of material, but it can be difficult to understand. This was her first time teaching, and it was at times difficult to understand. She has good exam reviews. Her review guide is very similar to the exam. She does genuinely care about her students/

The course material itself was fairly easy, but understanding the professor is a bit of a challenge. This was also her first time teaching the course, so maybe it was just a general nervousness or getting used to teaching the material. Prepare to teach yourself the material. Don't let this discourage you from taking this course.

analysis.name: Cecilia Ying
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is honestly so bad at teaching and the lectures are completely different from the recitations. The TAs don't know anything about what they're teaching and we're blindly expected to know what to do on the labs. The midterm was bad as well as the professor didn't even talk about 1/3 of the contents on it n now my GPA is suffering.

The lectures have almost nothing to do with the recitations. Lab grades didn't come out for 3 weeks, while we had already submitted another one. Doing iClicker in lecture, 80% of people were getting the questions wrong because they didn't know what she was talking about. I dropped bc I'm CODO'ing to HK & this class was a complete waste of my time.

No idea how she was hired by Purdue. Every other Professor I've had in Daniels is miles better. While the content in class itself was fairly easy, the grading system made no since. 40% of our grade was based of 4 random in class kahoots made from unspecified material. Other than the lab projects there was no hw. Purdue please hire someone else.

Total disconnect between lecture and lab. They feel like two different courses. The professor is detached from the lab, and TAs lack any passion for teaching. The lecture content is disorganized and has zero practical use for the lab. As a business major, this is the biggest waste of tuition at Purdue.

Class has a lot of potential. It's first year of the class(fall sem 2025)but there are flaws. The projects are overall interesting; you make your own chatbot agent for a local biz, good for resume and overall skills. The only coding we did was prompt engineering- we put into Gemini and it generates for us but we interpret. It's alright tbh take it.

analysis.name: Meng Cui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cui's lectures were very fast, but he did a good job explaining things and gave useful examples. Homework and exams had a few more difficult problems but were fair. My main issue was that we didn't have practice exams.

Cui is a great prof., he is very passionate and explains things thoroughly. However, he goes fast in lecture and has a thick accent so it is hard to understand him at first. The exams and material of 301 is very hard. However, prof. Cui is very inspirational, and works with students to help them understand the material.

He's an amazing professor for this class. He may have a thick accent and pretty bad handwriting, but he is so caring and really goes above and beyond to make sure every student understands. He goes at a good pace, goes over homework solutions and lecture reviews everyday, and he hand writes all of his notes (which I love). Great guy, I recommend!

Cui is a decent lecturer and I would consider him a safe choice if you don't have any good options. He has an accent but its not bad. His lectures are nothing special but he does a lot of practice problems which is nice, and responds via email decently quick, but wont care about any issues or conflicts you have, so expect no leniency.

He's not it. The lectures are the biggest waste of time. I have played an hour of clash royale in every single lecture this year. That being said, I know more about the material than anyone else I've met just because I only learn by myself. This means you only learn how not to do it by listening to professor Meng teach.

analysis.name: Jean Chmielewski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Chmeilewski is easily the best professor for taking organic chemistry. She made Orgo not just clear and straightforward, but interesting and even FUN. It's crazy how great she is. If you get her as a prof, you're in for a great semester. (Only complaint - she talks kind of quietly, even with a mic, so definitely sit in the front rows.)

Jean is absolutely amazing. The lectures have packets that you just pick up at the beginning of class and fill out. I don't see why you would want to skip her class, but in case you do--- don't. Organic Chem isn't a walk in the park, and just as a heads up, the first exam is the easiest one, but props. the one you'll do the worst in

Prof Jean has been the best chem professor I have ever had. She teaches at a good speed and provides not packets that are very helpful. Her exams are not too hard or long. The lectures and Psos don't have attendance because she respects students' ability to choose how to spend their time. You don't need to buy the model kit that she asks you to.

Amazing professor. She gives out handout at the start of every week. At the end of each chpt she gives you a bullet point list of things she want you to know. She also makes reaction maps and gives a great study packet for finals. Give out old exams as practice. All exams were fair, and she gives extra credit.

I love this professor with my whole heart and wish she taught all my classes. She made chemistry make sense and I'm SO mad they swapped professors halfway through. She's awesome. Throwback to that time she sawed a cooler in half to explain chirality.

analysis.name: Ronda Cassens
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ronda is a great person but when it comes down to it she simply cannot teach. We spent about 3 classes learning how to draw holds and hold entries and on the third day after her not teaching us properly for the last 2 classes, she shows us a 7 minute video which explained it perfectly.
Very hard class with hard professor to deal with.
Ronda is great as a person, but teaching is a little more difficult for her. Incredible human being but simply doesn't know how to effectively teach.

Ronda simply does not know how to engage or instruct a class. She uses slides and information that alone would not prepare a student for their commercial written or practical. I have never had such a sad experience in a class as I have had with Ronda.

Absolutely terrible professor. Ronda no idea how to teach. If you get her for a professor you should seriously consider finding tutoring or online help as she can't explain anything. Worst experience I've had at Purdue so far.

analysis.name: Christopher Munt
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Nothing could pull me into another class led by Professor Munt. I would change majors before sitting through another one of these classes. The whole class felt performative… it felt like he wanted us to be his adoring fans, and it never sat right with me. I got through it, but at the cost of some of my mental health. Received almost no feedback.

There was so much reading due each week and it often didn't relate that much to the class. Also there were a lot of long papers throughout the semester and I never received any real feedback on them. He seems really nice and caring but the way he structured the class made me dread going to it.

He was kind and caring but he assigned a lot of useless reading and unnecessarily long papers just to give zero useful feedback on them. The class content got boring and repetitive, and it became difficult to bring myself to go to this class towards the end of the semester.

The class wasn't hard, and the content was okay. There definitely wasn't enough substance to make me love it. Professor Munt was kind, but gives off a level of arrogance/self-importance that definitely dragged down his score for me. Fair grader, but definitely could have behaved less like royalty. Teach a class vs. basking the spotlight/attention.

Christopher is a really nice and easy to talk to professor. He seems genuinely interested in his students' voices, thoughts, and perspectives on issues revolving around the LGBTQ community. My only issue is that he takes forever to grade assignments so it's tough to predict your final grade.

analysis.name: Joseph (Kuan-Hua) Chen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 179 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Holy cow Dr. Chen is great. Actually had a different professor for Calc 3 and I skipped all of his lectures so I could watch Chen's lectures online. Great handwriting, explains things at a reasonable level and pace. Gave me an unreasonable standard to hold the rest of my professors to.

Prof Chen IS the Purdue Math department, despite having different professors along the way this man has carried me from MA 162 to MA 303 with his recorded lectures. His explanations and lectures are incredibly thorough and he explains in a way that resonates with many students. His exams can sometimes be tough, but are fair. Thank you Prof Chen!

Chenflix saved my life during math courses at purdue (162, 261, 266), and I've heard his in person lectures are even better. Very good at breaking topics down, explaining how to do them, and why we do them. Very efficient teaching style with not a lot of time being wasted too. Very easy to understand, one of the best professors at purdue.

Professor Chen is a great lecturer, not only for his ability to explain mathematical concepts in a clear way, but also his commitment to making his lectures accessible to other students. He does a great job at giving his students a strong intuition about how we model/solve differential equations. This intuition is easily applied to other courses.

Amazing professor. You can easily notice that he hard work that he puts into the class because he genuinely wants to see his students excel. He doesn't make things harder than they have to be. He explains everything thoroughly, clearly and makes even 7:30 classes worth going to.

analysis.name: Daniel Johnstone
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His teaching style is not the most exciting, but he the important bits across. If available, you should take Mummert instead, because he coordinates tests and therefore provides more up-to-date information. As a side note, Johnstone chews and drinks (dr. pepper and mountain dew) loudly in the microphone, which is a less than pleasant experience.

I didn't have many issues with him, he is open to criticism if he makes a mistake during a lecture and cares about his students. 

The difficultly comes from the exams and the quizzes. ChenFlix, Khan Academy, Professor Leonard (YT), and Paulsonlinemathnotes, were helpful in understanding the material. Hope you have a good TA and a big curve.

Prof. Johnstone was an incredible lecturer and makes abstract concepts understandable. The homeworks were long but the exams were forgiving. Make sure to read if you miss a lecture since the content builds on itself a lot. Quizzes could be resubmitted at any point for full credit, with VERY detailed feedback and hints. Overall a great class.

He teaches well enough that I did not have to review on Chenflix. I'm glad there are good lecture videos and no attendance is required. I don't think a "difficulty rating" is relevant for this professor because it's mostly the exams and TA graded quizzes which are the main difficulty points. Note that the homework takes a nonzero amount of time.

Johnstone is great. Lectures are super engaging. MA261 is very tough, so get ready for a LOT of out-of-class studying/prep. TBH, your grade in 261 heavily depends on your TA and exams. Johnstone is funny and simplifies concepts really well. His office hour sessions are also great. Take advantage of them! HW is heavy (2x/week) but doable. Good luck!

analysis.name: James Davis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Davis's lectures are incredible and there are a lot of connections he makes to the real world. He cares a lot about his students. However, the grading for the course is very slow given the amount of workload. Feedback is not given on time and grades have not been posted for anything, despite the end of the semester approaching.

No doubt at all, the best classroom experience I've ever had at Purdue. Dr. Davis does not teach in a "traditional" manner. He teaches his students in a result-oriented manner that actually preps you for the real industry/academia. He cares for his students, goes above and beyond to make sure that they make the most out of the course. Full points!
One of the best professors I've had at Purdue. Highly recommend taking any class offered by him

Davis was a pretty interesting professor for software engineering. He brought in several engaging speakers and has a lot of good experience and ideas to share. Classwork felt a little heavy at times and there wasn't a good way to rate groupmates who were behind on the project.

ECE 461 with professor Davis might be the best class I've taken at Purdue. His class is structured in a way that really help you get the feel for what an actual Software Engineering role might look like in industry and his lectures are just plain fun to attend.

analysis.name: Donald Pappas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Yes, BIOL 439 is VERY challenging especially compared to any other labs. But the reasoning is important. He treats us like adults who can think for ourselves, he wants us to learn and succeed and there are more than enough resources to do so. He devotes a huge amount of time and energy into making sure we have fun and learn a lot.

Dr. Pappas is an ineffective instructor. Success in this course requires extensive memorization of lecture quizzes rather than learning from lecture, which is often confusing and unhelpful. Exams consistently contained errors, and concerns were met with delayed or dismissive responses instead of meaningful support. Don't take BIOL221 w/ Dr. Pappas.

A fine professor, nothing special, but information is clear, though sometimes lecture can be info-dense. But, micro is already very difficult so not all him. Make sure to study like crazy; everything is extremely easy to study for if you give yourself time to do so. Lab is honestly more difficult to do well in than lecture, lab exams are impossible

The lecture portion of this course was actually quite easy. Focus on memorizing the bank of test questions he has for each lecture and explaining the learning objectives for the exams. He explains the lecture content quite well. I found the lab portion of the course to be much more difficult.

It's hard to respect a professor who creates his exams from a series of 400+ MC questions you need to memorize for each exam that probably hasn't been changed since 2022. He comes off kind but does not show effort in preparation of the course.

analysis.name: Daniel Kelly
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super easy class if you choose to have graded participation: basically, miss less than 7 classes by the end of the semester, and receive additional 5% to final grade. Also, posts all lecture notes online, which literally covers EVERYTHING you could possibly need for papers and tests. Easy A for a PHIL class

Best professor on campus if you want to take a philosophy course. Let's you have an additional 5% if you miss less than 7 classes which was nice. Super lenient with grading the written essays and exams. He gives you a list of questions that could come for the exam and only picks questions from there which was nice.

Easily one of my favorite professors at Purdue! Very engaging lectures, clearly passionate about the subject, encourages class discussions, and very responsive. Class is well organized, reading quizzes are easy, 3 blue book exams are simple, 3 writing assignments are generously graded. Great class, even better prof. DMFK all the way!

He's a really smart and interesting guy. There are 3 or 4 papers each semester and 2 essay style exams. He presents the material in a clear and enjoyable way. All of the tests are based on his lectures and he doesn't post the slides online, so you must attend class. The material was interesting, but the course did tend to drag on towards the end.

Professor Kelly was my favorite professor throughout my time at Purdue. I really enjoyed the structure of the class. The discussions were easy to get into, the topics were interesting, the workload was not overwhelming. I ended up looking forward to this class because of how well he ran it and how stress-free it felt.

analysis.name: Deepak Nadig
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is an amazing professor. He is kind, understanding and extremely helpful. As long as you explain what you are facing, he is very open to help you, give extensions. You will do great in class as long as you reach out for help. Probably one of the most understanding profs i've ever met at Purdue.

The course's lectures were exceptionally well-delivered andpacked with info and that made complex topics easily understandable. However the sheer amount of homework was quite a lot requiring a lot of time investment to keep up with. Overall, it's a highly educational experience for those willing to dedicate effort to reap the benefit.

The class covers a lot of topics and it is hard to connect them as they are wildly different. The course is meant to introduce different architectures and is mostly manageable. The learning experience under his instruction proves to be quite demanding. Some labs are easy but after the first few you need to know some linux to work on Pi projects.

I believe this class is the issue, not the professor. I'm sure he knows his stuff well but is not a good lecturer at all. Some of the labs make no sense and sometimes don't relate to the lectures at all. You have to get lucky with your TA, mine was terrible at grading and explaining. Extremely disorganized class if you don't know what you're doing.

Prof. Nadig is a nice person. He is incredibly intelligent and has done a lot of research in his field. That being said, he is a poor lecturer. His lectures are incredibly boring and it very hard to learn from him as he doesn't do a good job of explaining the concepts. The class itself is manageable but learning from him is difficult.

analysis.name: Nadya Dubikovsky
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class is easy but I have had two friends kicked out of her class for getting sick. she is not understanding about these things at all and does not accept doctors notes. you better be in the best health of your life while taking her class. she will make you take it again if you get the flu and are out for a week

Ms. Dubikovsky is a very kind and passionate professor. She is always willing to help students understand material and will help with any questions you may have. She is particular about attendance though. I don't believe you can learn the material for her class properly within being in class so I understand why she's so particular about it.

The class is easy but just know that excused, sick absences with doctors notes are still counted to your absences limit of 4. Don't waste your time getting a doctor's note if you are sick. The professor will not level with you if you have 4 absences even if you have doctors notes for them. Also, if you are 10 minutes late, you're marked absent.
A fantastic instructor. Grades you according to your existing skill level, so if you put effort in you'll be fine.
This class was actually not bad. As long as you attend class everyday and participate you will be fine. She sometimes plays favorites but overall she is very sweet and a decent professor.

analysis.name: Daniel Nowak
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: take anyone but him for this class his requirements are not clear whatsoever and most of the assignments that we do in class has nothing to do with marketing management. he does not lecture properly and the exam is built on very niche things where he says that there maybe multiple good answers but we have to pick the best one AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

Pretty harsh with grading, and there's lots of assignments that he never gets around to finishing so they just linger on Brightspace ungraded. You have to purchase access to this business simulation website for 60 bomboclat dollars and run trials with a team. He's chill most of the time but also incredibly unenthusiastic at presenting/lecturing.

Disorganized, unclear, and poorly run. Grades posted so late you never know where you stand. Midterm was 13 MCQ with 8 answers each in 20 min and felt designed to trick, not test. Teaching is outsourced to student debates and the syllabus totally ignored. Final project timing is unrealistic. Professor lacks basic course management skills. Avoid.

Very disorganized and difficult to learn from. Lectures are mostly random case studies with sloppy explanations and no slides or structured material to follow. It feels like you're teaching yourself most of the time. For a 7:30am class especially, the lack of organization makes it a waste of time. Would not recommend

Dr. Nowak is an awful professor. Do not take this class. He grades unfairly if you disagree with him, and missing more than two 7:30 AM classes drops you a letter grade. Most students scored under 40% on the midterm, and you must write a paper to get the curve. I would also like to say that 1-star reviews keep getting deleted- avoid at all costs.

analysis.name: David Nolte
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took 410 and 410 with him. Uses his own book which is exactly what he teach in the class, and both are not very helpful. Doesn't really answers the questions students asks (doesn't like being questioned repeatedly). Few questions on homework but they take forever. Grading is pretty easy though. He is basically the typical old physics professor.

(PHYS410 H Mech I is now defunct) For intermediate mechanics, Nolte teaches from his own textbook, which is adequate but not ideal (the good part is beyond the scope of a non-honors class). When answering questions, he tends to talk in circles until the questioner gives up. Class is difficult and time consuming, but the grading is generous.

He knows the material however seems to forget that his students are taking this course for the first time. Class average was consistently a D the entire semester. Very test heavy and likes to try to trip up students with his questions. Be ready to have to teach yourself and pay attention in the lectures. Avoid at all costs.

He is great at teaching the material and is very clear about the things you should expect on the exams and how to prepare for them. The class isn't easy but its very fair. If you do the work, go to lecture, and study, you'll do fine.
Hes a great professor but my god the homework and exams are long. Dont expect any plans over the weekend if you have them. Most do fine just the typical Purdue physics course

analysis.name: Danny Milisavljevic
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Given the inherent difficulty of the course material, he does a fantastic job of relaying the information in a way that is easy understand and apply. He does a good job of keeping the class engaged, and he does a great job of making lecture worth your time. If you attend and participate lecture and recitation you will do well in the course.

Prof Milisavljevic is a great professor, he teaches the material very well, and answers all questions thrown at him in lecture. He also gives about 2-3 iClicker questions each lecture, and normally reveals the answer before closing the poll so most people get it right. He also explains that iClicker for those that don't understand.

Everything about him is great, except his teaching style. He goes way too fast, sometimes to the extend that you find it hard to catch up with the material and end up being confused. I have taken two classes with him and this has happened every time. Lectures very content heavy.

Dr. Milisavljevic is ADORABLE and INCREDIBLE! He makes physics so much easier (but it's still hard, FYI), and will actually make you laugh in class. iClicker questions are attendance points, but he is flexible if you need to miss a day for a good reason! Study the past exams and the iClicker questions (LIKE REALLY DO THIS) and you'll be fine!

Honestly, he's gotta be the best physics professor I've had yet. He does his best to help out as much as he can, keeps the mood light, and teaches the material well. He's a pretty funny guy and cares about his students. No complaints at all here, only praise.

analysis.name: Evidence Matangi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super knowledgable! Gets through lectures quickly and cancels class a lot. Does a good job warning you about the tough parts of the exam. He is also very laid back with logistical stuff; and this class is not bad if you took AP stats. They made it less work compared to previous years. I think his rate my professor is super harsh.

I would argue that Dr. Matangi did the best he could under the conditions of the course. There is a lot of content, the course powerpoints are confusing, and there's little to no overlap between hw, computer assignments, and exams. The content isn't too difficult to teach to yourself and he was extremely helpful and kind outside of class.

He used another lecturer's slides and recordings for "quality-control purposes", but I believe he should have given lectures himself. For exams, we were told to type our work and answers into lockdown browser, but we were told that we could upload pictures after I had already submitted. There was a discussion forum that he almost never answered.

He was a very nice and passionate teacher. The lectures involved him mostly reading off of slides without many example problems, so you would have to learn on your own too. He's always open to help if you reach out to him though.

Does not teach, just reads out complicated math out of slides. You will have to learn to code in R by yourself, and its HARD. Additionally, no curve at all and exams are tough (cheat sheet allowed tho). Don't recmend.

analysis.name: Enrico Martinez
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Martinez is undoubtedly the worst CHE professor at Purdue. He messed up every student's final grade, and we cannot get them fixed until the end of next semester, so our GPAs are lower because of his mistake. His lectures are incoherent and he makes constant mistakes. No one learned a single thing from his lectures. Avoid him at all costs.

This course was a disorganized mess. The lecture schedule was largely ignored. Error-ridden announcements were frequently sent out causing mass confusion. Grading standards were unclear and inconsistent between TAs. Released laughably incorrect final grades for half of the class and missed the final grade submission deadline for the second half.

Martinez needs to retire ASAP. His lectures were unintelligible and on multiple occasions he taught office hours in Spanish. His grading was all over the place. He had TAs grade a certain number of whole exams with subjective grading rubrics. There were grade discrepancies that he knew about and disregarded. This class was a headache bc of him.

Simply put Martinez is too old to still be teaching. His lectures absolutely blew no matter when in the semester it was. Third exam was impossible, don't know anyone who scored above a 70. Gave us a week and a half to do a project that we were supposed to have available for at least 4 weeks. Do not take a class with him if you want happiness.

Martinez shouldn't be teaching. Lectures were hard to follow and constantly filled with wrong information. Homework was a huge time sink, mostly due to poor explanation of topics or topics not being covered altogether. Grading errors between TAs were known and ignored. Failed to input accurate final grades for the majority of the class.

analysis.name: Emily Easley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a regular instructor if you have this class and you don't need any help. Its an extremely easy course. However, if you need help with a serious situation that relates to you needing flexibility- she is empty headed who will smile and be fake to you, and make things extremely difficult even though you have documents.

She is super nice, and the class is pretty easy. Attendance is required, but lectures are fine for a one-credit hour. Barely any assignments, and the few there are were easy. She enjoys when students participate, but will never really force you to.
Professor Easley was a great professor. She provides a lot of helpful tips, and she makes the class easy. The few assignments are meant to help you for your future career.

Emily was good for MGMT 295. There is a lot of work for her class and she WILL NOT accept late work. Attendance is mandatory, points are taken off even if you have a doctors note with one drop. Points are also taken if she sees you on your phone. I learned a good amount from the course. She's chill, just do the work and come to class and your good.

This is fairly new class but she does not know what she is doing. The class is not very useful information but its an easy A mostly. Its mandatory attendance and she is very strict on phones and stuff while she is "teaching", which is literally just her reading off slides of things she got from somewhere else. Do group work every single day also.

analysis.name: Erin Britton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: When I finished presenting with my group, she told me my information was wrong and gave me a hard time about it. We looked it up after the presentation and I was in fact right. Even after all of this, she still said I was wrong. Take someone else she is a headache

she disorganized, unhelpful and made fun of presentations at the end of the semester. i think she really tried but she was new and i was just confused the whole time none of the information made sense and was usually wrong.
She is all over the place. Very disorganized, doesn't respond to emails. Always late to class. Her notes were nothing like the exams.

analysis.name: Eunsun Smith
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Smith is a nice lady but lowkey she does not know how to teach. I would go to her lectures and learn nothing, you have to teach yourself. Class is definitely disorganized, you have to know some Java before going into it. Overall class wasn't too bad, lab, in class assignments, quiz on the reading, and lecture reflections. 7:30 lecture sucked tho.

This professor jumped straight into stack and heap memory before understanding the basics of java. Very difficult to understand what the professor is trying to convey during lecture. Her "in class activities" are pointless and waste time with busy work (made me feel like I was back in middle school). Highly recommend acquiring the recommended book.

Teacher needs to restructure the programming class better and needs to remove the inclass assignment to make time to better explain the code/build it in class. Be prepare for sudden changes in the course due to emotionally fueled decisions.  Tread lightly and find outside resources.

Smith is the worst professor I have ever had at my time at Purdue. She cannot teach this simple Java class and refuses to post previous professors' teaching material to supplement her atrocious instruction style. She needs to get fired.
Continuously ends class 20-30 minutes early lacking content to teach, cancels class after student complaints, and refuses to answer some students' questions, and overall doesn't teach the class well.

analysis.name: Beth Hess
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Hess did great job with this course. Lectures were pretty engaging and useful. The course is well organized and deadlines are clear. No complaints.
Hess was super awesome. Most of the time in lectures there was either a guest speaker or a personal story, and all of the assignments were super easy.

290 is a really informative class. It's an easy A, but you learn a lot from the alumni who return to present at the seminar. The speakers are often inspiring and cover all types of industry within ME so its great for all students of all interests. Hess is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students and wants the best for them!
Prof. Hess has great examples and is very engaging for the students. She clearly cares about the students.

Course taken Fall 2024. Overall, it was the course that I didn't like overall. She was a pretty average professor, seemed monotonous and ok at lecturing, but it was an ok class, just sat there every week to get my attendance points, but it was fine.

analysis.name: Emily Dykhuizen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dykhuizen was knowledgable on the content but did move too slowly throughout her portion of the course. She was available outside of class for office hours, even during the parts of the semester when she wasn't the main professor. Definitely use the old quizzes/tests on brightspace as she follows the exact format.

She doesn't seem to have it all together, which only sometimes affected lectures. Most quiz and homework content from last year's were consistent with what we had this year (could become a bad crutch if you don't make an effort to understand the content). Easiest professor to understand from PHSC 204/MCMP 204.
She went thru the lecture slides nicely and gave pointers on how to remember certain things. It was very relaxing. Probably the best instructor out of the 3 mcmp204 instructors.
I had her for PHSC 204, and she is the sweetest person ever. I loved having her as my professor and would definitely want to have her again!
Dr. Dykhuizen gives you good information but doesn't do the best job explaining. I don't recommend going to her personal office hours unless you want to be criticized.

analysis.name: Eddy Efendy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very helpful and open to student's suggestions . Really wants the student to understand the materials. Very great class! I learnt a lot from it!

Heard this guy changed the way he teaches and I believe it if so many people struggled before. He did an amazing job getting me to understand statics where future professors just rush through everything. If you go to lecture you will understand it but if you don't then you will struggle. Great professor

Statics is challenging for me but he is helpful in labs and gives lots of extra credit and gives lots of credit for work shown on exams. Office hours weren't helpful because he just asked me to work with another student to figure out my question. Still recommend him and would take again.

Third time in the class, and still don't know what I'm doing. Does two examples in class that aren't related to the homework in any way. He also sits at the play place at the Tippecanoe Mall. I have photo evidence of that

Lectures are brutally boring but he is VERY helpful in lab and is willing to work with the class and is open to curving things if people ask. Will remove topics off exams if he feels he did not cover them good enough. He will check your lab work before you turn it in so you get a good grade. One of the better profs I've had, pretty hard to do bad.

analysis.name: Elise Frketich
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, this class is taught by the sweetest kindest most joyful professor in this god forsaken, freezing, featureless, hell hole. Dr. Starr is amazing!! She was my lecturer for the second half of CHM115 and it's so evident that she's dedicated to her students learning the material! She gives lots of practice problems in class that mimic exam questions, answers questions really clearly, and is so down to earth and passionate! Definitely would recommend!!

I LOVE Steve. He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He truly cares about the subjects he teaches and his students. He makes classes fun while ensuring that you learn. I wish he could be my professor for all of my classes and cannot wait to have him again next semester.
Take his classes if you get the chance

Attendance is graded for CORRECTNESS as it covers the last lecture or even content from the lecture learned that day. DO NOT TAKE!

Was not very willing to explain how improvement can be made. Very memorization-heavy, exams are extremely difficult (50/50 multiple choice and free response), and homework from her website is rambling on and does not get to the point she is attempting to make. I would suggest taking this class somewhere else, if possible.

He is a good lecturer, funny, and keeps the class interested. Loved his attitude. Would recommend him for this course. Text is never used to read but has all the homework in it. Prepare to have homework every class.

Really unnecessarily difficult. Take literally any other eaps 100-level course. There's hours of lecture and readings every week and the homework is unnecessarily time consuming for what the class is. It's really not bad, but compared to the other intro eaps classes it is ridiculous.

analysis.name: John Morgan

Professor Morgan writes purposefully vague and almost incomplete practice and exam questions that require assumptions, guesswork, and clarifications. He taught with Prof. Liu and while Liu will make sure to re-explain a difficult topic when a student asks a question, Morgan seems to give up. He is condescending when you ask him questions.

Professor Morgan gets a lot of slack, but I believe it is just because 205 is a difficult course. He is a caring professor, who is great at explaining difficult concepts. He is always helpful in office hours when you ask good questions. And you can always email him for additional help. I appreciate his effort and care he puts into it all.

Professor Morgan is very poor at lecturing and tends to not go into very much detail when doing example problems, skipping over key steps assuming that his students already understand how to do the problem. The homework in this class is the only way to truly learn the material, make sure you do all the problems and read the textbook to pass.

analysis.name: Qi Guo

review_highlights.comment: I took 301 under Professor Guo. Solid teacher, makes sure to pause for questions. Quizzes that he had were fair and takes very neat lecture notes in class. Overall would recommend to take 301 under Guo.

One of the best prof I've had at Purdue, and the best choice for 301. Exams are brutally hard but each exam is curved to a 75 average, and the class is curved ~10% on top of it! Beautiful lecture slides, and recorded! As long as you work hard and honestly, you will do well. If you have the option to take it with Guo - run, don't walk!

Very good professor who truly cares about student's learning. Lectures are engaging and he takes time to make sure the class is keeping up with him and to answer questions. Homework take a significant amount of time but exams are very similar to them. Exams are curved to 75%

301 is a tough class, and professor Guo was awesome at both making concepts easy to understand and the class fun and engaging. He's a super genuine person who truly cares about his students. I guess you could say that he's a *Guo*ted professor :^)

analysis.name: Kent Quanrud
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Generous curve. I did perfect on homeworks and exactly average on exams and ended with A-. Super friendly and helpful and accessible outside class. Really cares about you. Best prof I've had at Purdue. Very knowledgable and inspiring.

He teaches well and breaks down the concepts into smaller chunks, but everything else in this class is poor. He has his own textbook, which is riddled with math errors (good luck studying). Both HWs and Exams use only problems from the textbook. There is no diversity in assessing you. You have to grade your own HW, which the TA evaluates!?!

This 3-credit course is actually a 9-credit course in disguise: Probability and Random Processes, Algebraic Graph Theory, and Algorithm Design. Everything is so intertwined that it makes the material much harder to master. 
While the instructor is patient and passionate about teaching, the course pacing is simply indigestible.

Professor Quanrud is a great lecturer, and the class was enjoyable. There were a few hiccups (errors in the textbook, self-grading policy, etc.) but overall the course was well worth it. Would recommend taking a class with him in the future.

Look at the trend in Kent's reviews, undergrads complain bc his class is hard, and grad students unanimously love him. The reality is he teaches a hard topic, but he actually makes it intuitive. Beyond that, he's one of the most abundantly caring and available CS professors I had at Purdue, he's the kind of person who it is impossible to dislike

analysis.name: Xiaokang Qiu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Actually the worst professor I've had at Purdue. The lectures make no sense and the course is very disorganized. The source code has bugs in it that make your work twice as difficult, and he can't debug his own code (it's another professor's work that he pawns off as his own, he couldn't be bothered to put in effort). Do not take compilers w/ him.

The professor attacks you if you ask for an extension even though he didn't even release the assignment until much later. So in order to keep the original due dates, he makes 2 steps due the same week. He is condescending and will constantly remind you that you have poor time management skills even though it's his fault.

Tough course, graded by 12 quizzes (+1 dropped). Some quizzes rocked, others sucked horrifically. Inconsistent, either breezed through slides or took forever to explain one thing. I would appreciate the addition of programming assignments to lessen the impact of bad quiz grades.

During the lecture, he cannot explain everything clearly, his slides make no sense, and you can't really learn from his lecture. His project is a disaster, you have to debug for him(takes about a day) since his code is pretty buggy and I bet he didn't test his code before he publish it to the class. (Maybe he just can't find or fix his bug^^)

His lectures are not very helpful, and he comes off as insensitive and condescending to students. One student asks him for clear instructions on project on Piazza, he replied "we didn't mean to babysit." You should know what you're getting into before taking his 468/595/573, they're basically the same class, but you need to do more in 573.

analysis.name: Tiantian Qin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
