review_highlights.comment: Talks very fast, impossible to keep up.  Does not explain concepts well, or how to use the online software.  Both in class & the recorded online lectures she skips steps, omits calculations, moves too quickly, & does not explain what she is doing so that students can understand. Take 501 with Tadd Colver instead, SAS sucks, but he is way better.

Before coming into this class i had a working knowledge of statistics. After leaving i can honestly say i have no idea what i am doing. Professor Qin does a poor job of wording her thoughts, has no organization in her lecture, and moves insanely fast through difficult subject matter. When asked to clarify she often confuses the entire class more.

She seems to be motivated, but she makes her students feel desperate. The biggest problem is that she skipped many procedures required for the student to study for review or preview. Another problem is that her midterm is too difficult to solve in time. If solving the questions had been worthwhile, I would have not felt frustrated.

Do not take this course.  I spend 10+ hours per week on the homework.  The online book is difficult to navigate and doesn't align well with the class powerpoints.  The instructor moves way too quickly.   Worst course I've taken at Purdue.

This professor is knowledgeable in statistics, but could not be worse at teaching the material in a manor that is accessible or understandable. The majority of time in class is spent in confusion. If you want to bond with other students over just how confused you are, this is the class for you!

analysis.name: Qifan Song
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He talks to the screen most of the class. Doesn't check if the class has understood the concepts or not.  He needs to improve his English fluency to teach and communicate well.  There's hardly any point taking this class if most of the time you are trying to decipher what he is saying

I signed up for this class and had to drop it. First of all, this professor's ability to explain the material is very limited. It is extremely difficult to follow his lectures. Also, he has a very thick accent. I am not a native speaker as well and I don't judge people easily, but I can easily say that he cannot communicate with the class at all.

Had him for a seminar class. Grade was basically entirely attendance (No A if you miss like 2 classes) and completion grades. Felt like a waste of time and you could tell he didn't really want to be there. Also talked quietly without a mic and is kinda hard to understand (OK English).

Dr. Song was very thorough in his lectures. He was prompt in his responses, reasonable to requests, and fair. I enjoyed his class. Other students may have had a negative experience with the content, but he did a good job making it easier to digest.
Classes are not very helpful, the textbook is much clearer. Exams and homework are easy, but homework is time-intensive (6-8 hours per week). Grading is lenient.

analysis.name: Qianlai Zhuang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was by far the most easiest class I have ever taken. Most of the times I forget I enrolled in this course. Your grades are dependent of quizzes, discussion posts and responding to 2 people. I never used the textbook, however, theres bonus points for buying it. Again, really easy class. Keep in mind, the prof and the TA barely answer your email

Lots of homework, group discussion is graded based on your English level and your grammar, makes this class like a English course, except his English is too poor to be a English teacher. and the topic he gave us were posted 2 years ago. For circuit he will only give you one day to finish, if you miss one section of circuit, you lose all credits.

This was one of the easiest classes I have taken so far. It was an online course. Each week consisted of a short essay submitted via blackboard and then feedback to two other classmates. Super easy! There were 8 quizzes. These were a little difficult and I think some questions on the quizzes were never in the reading. Extra credit helps!

This was the easiest course I ever took. There were weekly quizzes, weekly discussion posts, and a final exam. The quizzes were all easy and directly based on the textbook. My only complaints were that the due dates were confusing and I had to buy a $95 textbook.
Very interesting topics! Complete the work on time and you'll get an easy A!

analysis.name: Pam Porterfield
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 198 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Pam rambles a lot with her examples which are incomparable to homework. She consistently exceeds the class time. Her exams are NOTHING like the practice exams. EA's are not helpful and tedious. No curve even though the exam averages are around 50%. Recitations are useless. TA's have no idea what is going on and what Pam is doing. AVOID THIS CLASS!!

She sets you up to fail.  I did fine, but the tests are not a measure of your intelligence, they are a measure of your ability to rapidly regurgitate information on your sheet.  If the professor is somehow reading this, allow more time for test or shorten them, I know students who studied for hours and hours and knew the material who failed.

Lectures felt like her stating information rather than truly explaining it. Prof. Porterfield is notorious for gatekeeping resources, such as complete lecture slides or answers to review problems. You get to make a cheat sheet for exams though. To (barely) succeed, take time out of class to work on understanding the material.

I took this class online, so no clue how to do excel activities. Not allowed to go to in-person recitations because "the roof may fall in." Sentiment towards her is validated by her treatment of students- made one cry. I completed the evaluation weeks before due, submitted it a few hours late and she took 50%. (due finals week) Good luck with her.

This class is not too good. If you were great at AP stats, things will be great but if not, this class is difficult. The average on our second exam was a 67. She emphasizes the use of Excel but we can't actually use it on exams so it's conflicting. I recommend watching the prerecorded lecture videos instead of boilercast or going to class.

analysis.name: Ruqi Zhang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

I have never been more offended by how a class was such a waste of time. I have learned literally nothing in this class. Way better off taking CS 573 instead of 578. she doesnt use a textbook, and intentionally leaves proofs off her slides so you have to show up. class is overly focused on theoretical side of things, so you never actually learn how to use models or compare them. i'm almost convinced that this is the most useless waste of a class in the CS dept, except that compilers also exists, so its close

analysis.name: Raji Sundararajan Sundararajan

taken 3 of her classes and will soon take a 4th. Professor Raji initially can seem hard to get along with but if you take the time to get know her she is a very caring person. This is the worst professor I have ever had. Refuses to answer questions and laughs at students for not understanding content. Easily one of the worst professors I have ever had. Very bad speaking skills, mumbles every other word, clearly is being forced to teach. She lost a students lab sheet and gave him a zero. analysis.name: Sally Ray

I could not have done it without her help in office hours, where she was more than happy to reexplain topics.

Knows her stuff well. All tests and quizzes are open ended with partial credit; but very easy to mess up. She makes the class sound easier than it is on the first day and sometimes does not explain concepts well or will just skip to the math. Her math is very good and clear though and she overall is a very good and caring professor.

Sally Ray is one of, if not, the best professor at Purdue. She is very caring and is very accessible outside of class. If you are unable to make it to her office hours, she will try and setup someone other time to meet, in-person or on zoom.

The class itself is interesting and the material builds on itself a lot. Get the basics down well.

10/10

Sally is salt of the Earth. She is truly one of the most caring instructors you will find. She is so approachable and wants to get to know all of us. Very easy to ask questions and responds quickly. She truly cares about our success and loves the material. Very big Purdue fan too! Funny and just plain awesome!

Professor Ray in an exceptional professor, she is good with explaining concepts and if you have questions she is always willing to help out during office hours. MA 373 is a challenging course but with practice and repetition the content is manageable. Always go to lecture, as some have said, notes are not posted online.

Most hard-grading professor at Krannert

This class has relatively no application outside of MGMT382. If you aren't an amazing note taker good luck. He provides no practice exam or study guides for the exams. This professor is bad. I dont know if its cause he has nothing to do but he will ensure you also have nothing to do but his work. His class is a 9-5 with himself saying its an "internship". Exams on New Year's Eve instead of being able to spend time with family cause he is miserable. Terribly spaced exams and homework.

analysis.name: Scott Sorensen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He can be monotoned, but he is extremely helpful and very understanding. I had a situation during my exam, and he was extremely helpful, making me clam down and still have time to finish my exam. He wants to be an actual professor and knows students have situations so he helps rather than punishes them for being human beings.

Overall Scott is a great professor. He cares about his students a lot and wants them to succeed. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives extra credit if you come. The class if a little dry but its ok. I didn't do so well on the first exam but was able to bounce back by completing his practice exams and ask questions in class. Take him for MGMT 201

For everyone saying that he is a "terrible professor", they are upset that they have to put in effort for a class. Yes, he is dry, but he truly does care about his students. He's real down to Earth and will ALWAYS answer any questions you have. His exams aren't too bad if you do the Foundational 15 and Review Problems he gives you as practice. 5/5.
This guy is THE GOAT. Scott is amazing in every way possible. He actually saved my dog from a burning building while simultaneously lecturing about MGMT 201. What a guy.

Sorensen is a very caring professor who wants his students to succeed.  He is very accessible if you ever have a question and he provides extra credit for attendance.  Accounting is a subject that is hard to make interesting, but I think he does a good job presenting the material in a very straightforward manner.

analysis.name: Gustavo Rodriguez-Rivera

review_highlights.comment: The best professor at Purdue, end of story.

Take GRR if you want to pass, but if you want to actually learn, find other ways.

Gustavo makes the course easier than Turkstra does, but this semester, his exams have been very unforgiving (the midterm more so than the final). There is very little you can do to know which multiple-choice topics will show up on exams, and he does little to help students prepare for them.

The main thing saving Gustavo is that he clearly cares a lot about the student's success and as such extends deadlines, makes exams easier, and gives extra credit. However, the lectures are abysmal, the projects and slides haven't been updated since 2001, and the TAs have no idea what he wants either. The class is just uninteresting and unorganized

When you take a class with a professor who cares for the success of their students, and who makes the class a space to enjoy learning, it becomes a safe space to learn. This guy could not be further from that. This guy hates seeing his students happy. His emails about cheat sheet restrictions look like trump tweets. #putthefriesinthebag.

analysis.name: Shuyi Weng
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment:
For context, I already had a 5 in Calc BC in hs.

For every unit besides series, I feel he taught it extremely well and concisely. He derives everything before giving you the formula to connect the pieces in your head. His notes are very organized, too.

His tests are extremely difficult and concept-heavy, so don't fall behind. Stay consistent!

Dr. Weng is by far the best professor I have ever had at Purdue. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and it is abundantly clear that he truly enjoys his work. I can tell that he is a professor not only focused on research, but also deeply committed to making a meaningful impact on undergraduate students. I would 100% take any class taught by him.

Calc 2 is a hard class but Shuyi is the goat. His teaching skill is on the level of the esteemed Chen from Chenflix - he manages to introduce all of the weird calc 2 topics in a way you can understand, which is not an easy task. Also his enthusiasm will make you actually want to show up to lecture even though he doesn't take attendance.

He's nice and funny, and he's a good teacher. However he's not great at making tests. I would go through all the study materials, and half the questions in the exams are phrased so awkwardly and unsimilar to study materials, which made them way harder. Plus, the average on the final was a a fifty and the curve was five percent

DO NOT USE THE RMP SCORE TO JUDGE HOW HARD THE CLASS IS. This class is unreasonably hard, sometimes making me question if they want to teach the material or your reading skills. Lectures are pretty ok. Recitation barely helps, and quizzes suck. Past exams don't reflect difficulty of exams. Read lecture notes carefully and use hw to study. good luck

analysis.name: Stacy Zuelly
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zuelly is an amazing professor, and I highly recommend taking her classes. Attendance is mandatory, but if you don't have any absences, you are able to opt out of the final exam! At the end of each lecture and lab there is a mini quiz, and if you paid attention during class, you will be fine!

Professor Zuelly's class had clear expectations and was not difficult. It was nice to not have final exams with 100% attendance throughout the semester as well. I was not a fan of her as a person. She has a lot of grace for herself and her own mistakes (which happen a lot) but is very strict on her students. Class is easy, but she's not kind.

This class was pretty easy but not very lax on any missing attendance. Attendance is required and there are NO drops or points that you can earn back for missing class. Zuelly is very funny, and I really enjoyed her class, but you really cannot miss much before your grade starts going down.

Just go to class!! Attendance is very important but it definitely pays off bc she makes it very clear what you need to know for the exams. If you pay attention and put the time into studying with the resources she provides, you'll be perfectly fine!

Fun and chill, but unorganized with unclear or last-minute group project requirements. But, she is an easy grader and lets the class be fun. Not the best for in depth learning but a laid back professor.

Focus on the exams and keep up with him in lecture and you will be fine

SWITCH LECTURES ASAP

analysis.name: James Tanoos

Dr. Tanoos is a passionate and goofy instructor and I really enjoyed taking his classes. Excellent Professor.  Dr. Tanoos is very well organized and efficient with classtime.  He's also willing and available outside of class to help students with their careers.  I gained several unique resume boosters through the semester that will be impressive to possible employers.  Definitely one of the better classes across campus.

analysis.name: Johnny Condori Uribe

Worst professor I have ever had throughout my 4 years at school. Lectures were just him writing out definitions and theorems and proofs- not super helpful.

analysis.name: Pramey Upadhyaya

He recorded his lectures,broke down concepts slowly, worked out examples, and even did supplementary recordings when students had questions. His explanations really made things click, even if the test material was hard

He is by far one of the nicest professors I have ever had. He is extremely accessible outside the class and is very approachable. His teaching pace is also perfect and you will understand everything clearly if you pay attention. He doesnt mind slowing down and repeating concepts should people need him to. Get this professor, you wont regret it!

analysis.name: Ryan Umbeck

Even during a 7:30am class, he still brought energy and engagement to each lecture that made the content easy to follow and understand. The course material can get a little confusing at times, but Dr. Umbeck goes over everything in great detail and answers questions perfectly.

Making an entry-level statistical inference course interesting is a very difficult task, but Professor Umbeck has a bright and encouraging energy that makes you want to pay attention simply out of respect for the effort he is putting into making the material understandable. Fantastic person, gives great feedback on issues with Stata HW (use him!).

One of the nicest professors at Purdue and teaches really well because he genuinely cares about the subject.
One of the best professor in Purdue. Always patient to students, answer questions on time.

analysis.name: John Umbeck

analysis.name: Terra Maienbrook
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

S/O to her TAs this semester (Nathan and Joseph) too!

There are three tests that make up 60% of the grade in total (15, 20, 25) but the last is the final exam, studying should get you at least a B on each. 2. Fun: actually makes accounting sound interesting, lectures are engaging, and so on.

Best MGMT200 professor. She is incredibly knowledgable in her field and her lectures make that obvious. Conveys the information of the class very clearly, keeps lectures engaging, and is always open to taking questions. Provides opportunities for easy extra points, just show up to class. Exams are incredibly fair, final is not cumulative.

Maienbrook is clearly knowledgeable about what she teaches. The class is well-structured, and there are plenty of extra-credit opportunities. She is also very approachable and offers flexible office hours. If you show up to class and actually do the homework, you're bound for success.

analysis.name: Christopher Uyeda

Uyeda is a WONDERFUL professor.  Easily my favorite so far at Purdue. Really good professor!  I was scared to take orgo, but he explains everything in a straightforward manner so it's really easy to understand.  He also spends the first couple of minutes reviewing material from the previous class which doesn't seem important but it's a really nice touch!

Professor White is the GOAT, I would drop any class to take his class.

Despite knowing that students in other 102 classes didn't have pop-quizzes, I would never have wanted a different professor for my 102 class. He may randomly call on you and you will be pushed out of your comfort-zone, but thats just Professor White.

She is one of the worst professors I have had at Purdue. She expects that we already have a knowledge on the topic even though its a beginning level class. She's hard to understand at times and everyone I know dreads going to her class.

analysis.name: Zahra Tehrani

The seminar can summarized as: read a research paper, hear a lecture, and fill out a couple easy questions. The problem? The papers were all basically the same. While I think that Dr. Tehrani might be a good professor, there was no reason to have this many reading assignments for a 1-credit class. It was way too information heavy for an 8-week course, especially if you aren;t interested in what she is teaching about.

Dr. Nyssa is hands down my favorite professor I've ever had. Her Technology and Culture class was extremely interesting and I enjoyed every lecture she gave. Random quizzes.

For instance, he was not able to finish a lot of topics that I felt like this class was just like introduction to fluid mechanics.

Intelligent, caring and funny prof - but busy and absentminded - I felt like he made a lot of mistakes during lectures. Exam problems were easier than HW. Use Panton's book and Fox and McDonalds', to learn concepts.

This professor could teach a rock how to swim. Lectures also conceptual, not just math, so you understand topic better. HW and practice exams help gauge understanding before exams. Answers emails promptly and is accessible outside of class. Cons: slightly unorganized, wish there were more example problems in lecture. Definitely would take again!
Professor Morris was a great lecturer and explained all concepts and solution methods clearly. He spends time to ensure students understand how to solve problems

analysis.name: Abdul Salam

Lectures can be very difficult to understand because Salam doesn't project his voice or enunciate. Deadman makes all the exams, many students didn't do well on the first exam because they didn't understand lecture content that Salam was responsible for.
Can't understand a single thing he's trying to teach and have never seen a professor whoop out a rate my professor for mid-semester feedback evaluation lol

Compared to Professor Deadman (a co-lecturer), Salam is a less competent lecturer and is not as engaging during lecture. Pauses for about 0.2 seconds to ask for questions, but simultaneously moves through slides at a snails pace.

Okay, to be honest, I have not and do not care about this professor enough to leave a review until he STOPPED US IN THE MIDDLE OF CLASS to review him so here I am. He is perfectly mild mannered. The middle of the road in enthusiasm for the subject he is teaching. The saltine cracker of teaching styles. I have more to say but I must keep this short.

analysis.name: Ronald Agyei

I had to teach myself the lecture content in order to do the homework, because by mid-semester he was 2 weeks behind in lecture. Gives negative points for incorrect multiple choice answers on the exams. Claimed the class wouldn't be curved but then made the final so hard that he had to curve by 5%.

He is clear, cares about learning, and explains concepts well. But the course was overly difficult for a class on beam bending. First exam had unfamiliar setups and too many calcs, no one finished, so he added 20%. The second was more fair but too long; average was failing, 20% extra credit assignment was offered. The fair final allowed me to pass

Prof. Agyei is a decent lecturer, however, he presents the content in an incredibly bland way making this class unbearably boring. His exams are often needlessly tricky and have problems that test knowledge not directly discussed in class. Attendance is also required which sucks because listening to the boring lectures at 9:00 am is insufferable.

man he is so boring I couldn't take it. And required attendance. He was pretty clear in explaining though. But hw and exams were just strangely tough or a stretch past lecture content. He was much better than the other professor of the semester though. I felt bad bc no one laughed at his jokes, no one paid attention.

Professor Agyei is very passionate about the material and it does help in learning it. The only issue is the material is kinda boring so his passion can only take you so far. Lectures were very helpful. I think exams were a little too hard imo based on the practice exams and homework, but office hours would definitely equip you to succeed.

analysis.name: Ruben Aguilar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved taking this class with Dr Aguilar. The lectures are setup in a way that's very unusual in that there are very few words on the slides but they were so easy to follow and the pacing didn't feel like information was being shoved down my throat. He took time to thoroughly answer questions and was always very friendly and wholesome

The course is laid out pretty understandably and the expectations are set on day one. The lectures are very informative and while attendance is not required it is great to be in the course and meet the professor who is a genuinely great and respectful academic. 10/10 course as long as you take the time to learn and question.
Thank you for your lectures and exposure you gave me all through your teachings.

He's a solid professor. Lectures are short and easy to understand. Not much work required for the class and extra credit is offered. Pretty easy to earn an 'A' if you watch the lectures and have access to the textbook.

He teaches the worst class I've ever taken. Literally five grades in the book. 4 20 point quizzes, 1 essay, and one 120 point final exam. The quizzes are over several lectures yet consist of two, page long, essay questions. He does not tell you what topic they are over. He does not give your quizzes back, so you don't even know what you missed.

analysis.name: Jeanette Aguilar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Nicest woman ever. The course is a lot of work but she made my life a little easier. Easily approachable and easy to talk to. Short lectures and lots of working time. She is the best.

An absolute gem. 5.0 is an understatement. She is extremely generous, helpful and flexible, and gives great but brief lectures in a way there will still be a good amount of time to work on assignments in class. She walks around class proactively offering help, giving solid advice and feedback. Getting her for 132 next semester is my top priority.

Professor Aguilar is very kind and energetic. She genuinely cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Her teaching team and herself do a great job at interacting with the students to ensure we understand the content and can complete difficult assignments. Mostly uses class time to work on homework assignments or group projects.

Aguilar is the best 131 teacher. Extremely caring and always open to trying to help her students learn while actually understanding the material. This class in general has a heavy work load for a 2 credit hour class, but having Aguilar definitely made this class easier compared to other professors.

She's super sweet and understanding, and clearly loves what she does. There was a snowstorm that prevented me from getting to campus safely, and she understood and allowed me to virtually do my work that week. The only thing is she's a little hard to understand at times due to her accent, but otherwise an awesome professor.

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bodony is a great conductor and gives very clear, concise feedback. He makes a lot of jokes in rehearsals and has a deep knowledge of musical history.

College is not easy for many, and he makes it known that he is there for his students. He is a great leader for the orchestras and music department as a whole.

Professor Bodony is a great orchestra director, and I really enjoyed all of the rehearsals. He is a very good conductor, and I like the advice he gives to make our pieces sound better. Show up to class (that is what your graded on) and enjoy.

I wanted to continue playing violin so I signed up for orchestra. Bodony does a good job picking fun music to play and providing helpful feedback, but I don't feel passionate about playing my instrument. I like that you're not graded for how well you perform so there's no pressure but sometimes that extra push can make music all the more rewarding.

Professor Bodony is an amazing guy. In the chaos of the coronavirus, he has been nothing but caring and understanding of how weird everything is for us right now. The first day of the semester, he gave a speech that made me tear up - acknowledging that our lives are strange right now, but as musicians we have the ability to escape through music

analysis.name: Jacob Adler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My only qualm with this class is that your grade is heavily dependent on what TA you have. I've heard great things about some TAs, while I had one would tell us blatantly wrong information. The lab itself is incredibly easy and as long as you try you will get an A. Make sure you have a good lab group or you will do a lot of extra work.

I am currently a freshman in bio 135 and 121 and Professor Jacob is a great professor. While the lab is mostly ran by TA/TIs, the lecture is ran by Jacob. All of the teaching team is amazing and wants you to succeed. My best advice is to show up for class and ask questions when you have them. Overall both courses are great!!!

Had JJ Adler for both bio 121 and bio 135. Really cares about his students, both academically and personally. He even sends personalized follow-up emails to your questions/concerns in forms. Lectures are clear 99% of the time. No textbooks. Only bad thing is you have to go "feasting with faculty" for office hours instead of normal office hours.

The learning goals could have gone better, and the criteria could have been clearly. The DNA analysis weeks were cool, but dirt is kind of boring. Overall the course was designed with good intentions but didn't have great execution. Good intro to college biology lab but glad to be done.

Dr. Adler is incredibly sweet and caring, but I have also heard that when it comes to grading, this class is very TA dependent. My TAs were nice, but some on Reddit mention how it felt like their TAs were out to get them. Make sure to attend the lectures and labs, reach out to Dr. Alder if you are struggling, and genuinely put in effort!

analysis.name: Adeola Mobolaji
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Mobolaji was the best professor I have had at Purdue so far. He is so passionate about the course and knows that most of us are there just because it's required so his main goal is "just listen to your classmates and learn." (He says that a lot). It's hard not to get an A in this course. Take him if you can get him!

Professor Mobolaji is super chill and always happy. He really wants the best for his students, and he is very understanding of his students. He grades super easy and gives amazing feedback. He lets students re-do presentations with no penalty if they blank the first time. He promotes a fun and stress-free environment. He is a great com professor.

Class was organized despite a few last minute changes. Lots of busy work assignments with few that are actually going to make you better at presentations. Finding live audiences is a bit of a hassle so make sure to be ready.
Very easy class and even nicer professor. Makes coming to class enjoyable and will respect your time and values. I would recommend taking any class that he teaches.

He truly represents what every teacher should strive to be. He cares about each students improvement and makes a direct effort to connect with all those in his class. He is my favorite professor on my schedule. Best guy!

analysis.name: Adam Wasserman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was very open to feedback and was accessible outside of class. He did give quizzes every Friday, so participation is mandatory on Fridays. However, his lectures were very engaging and you could tell he is very passionate in his work. Additionally, he was understanding of our stresses, such as having a Friday quiz during an exam week

Great lectures and a really well organized and paced class. The grading scale is also very forgiving. The only frustrating element of the class was having to get up at 8:30 for lectures. Overall incredible class.

Love love love Wasserman. He's so kind and you can tell he cares so much about the students. You need an 85% to get an A, with 3-4 dropped quizzes and either 1 dropped midterm or half-dropped final. Only necessary attendance is Friday quizzes, every week. Would recommend actually doing the reading, but it's not checked. Overall loved the class!

Dr. Wasserman is da GOAT. He wants to get to know and his lectures have amazing demos and clear notes. You only need an 85 to get an A and he lets you drop 4 quizzes, 1 midterm or half the final, and 1 lab. Dr. Wasserman sets you up very well for higher level chem no matter if you plan to go into grad, medical, dental, or whatever career!

Dr. Wasserman was probably one of my favorite professors this semester. He's really creative with his lectures and is happy to answer any questions that his students have. The only thing that gets me are the Friday quizzes, which can be a bit stressful at times to prepare for. There's a lot of outside work, however. But Wasserman is awesome!

analysis.name: Adam Kotanko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Most caring professor I've ever had. You attend class and email your group's discussion summary for credit every class (hence "mandatory" attendance). You get plenty skips for when you're sick, and he provides extensive feedback on your submissions. He has a passion in teaching and is a very understanding instructor. Very light coursework.

He's a great teacher that doesn't believe in exams/quizzes, but rather testing through group discussions, projects, and film reviews. In fact, he is just a grad student, but compared to my friends who had full professors that just lectured and gave exams, I still learned way more. If you take Mr. Kotanko he will make you a better person.

Kotanko is an extremely kind and understanding professor. He prompts you to think beyond the surface-level appearance of society. He has great communication and his respect for his students is evident. I would love the chance to take one of his classes again.

This is the best professor at Purdue. He is so caring and genuinely gets to know each of his students. He is understanding and wants to see you succeed. He is not a hard grader at all. This is the best professor and class ever.

Seriously the sweetest professor I've ever had. This is a really easy class the only way you'll fall behind is if you skip a lot of classes. Technically attendance isn't mandatory (if you're really sick he'll understand) but points are given for discussions so you really have to pay attention to those but you can always make them up. 4 get dropped.

analysis.name: Adam Huffield

Adam shared good info from his experience as an RD in the "real world."

I took Dr. Watkins "Homegrown" class this last fall semester, as well as taking one of his HONR 19901 classes. He is such a wonderful teacher, and he genuinely cares about his students. I had no problem with coming to his office hours with my questions about his assignments, and he always gave back clear feedback and made everything make sense.

Lectures are very one-sided, as he tends to be very insistent on his own viewpoints, despite preaching being affirmative and open-minded. He gives very unclear feedback, and is an unnecessarily harsh grader for it being a 1 credit class, taking off points without indicating why just because he can't bring himself to give someone a 100%.
Very respectful, very kind. This class requires a lot of participation. He provides articles to read, but no purchases necessary. Really will help your leadership grow. Not a difficult class.

review_highlights.comment: This professor can be disorganized, but is incredibly intelligent, helpful, energetic about the material, and a joy to work with. Thanks to her, I worked twice as hard as other MA students I knew, but the final result was worth it. Thanks April!!

This class was very informative.  It had excellent coverage and a good pace.  I would recommend it for anyone who is interested in any type of language testing - including writing exams for your own classes.
She is a great mentor and supervisor. She's straightforward and offers good constructive comments all the time. I would highly recommend her as an adviser and teacher.

analysis.name: Amanda Manning
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amanda Manning is the best instructor I have had at Purdue. Her lectures are so straightforward, and her teaching style is amazing. She genuinely cared about each and every student and took the time to learn everyone's name. Office hours are helpful if you're ever struggling. If you can take her section, I highly recommend it!!

The attendance points dont really matter cause theyre 2/2, but if youre not good at math and dont go to class often you will be behind. The tests are 12 multiple choice worth 8 pts each so you gotta lock in. Make sure to do good on the first exam so you dont dig a hole for yourself right away (thats what I did). Also try not to cheat on homework.

Amanda Manning is an awesome teacher! It is obvious that she is passionate about everyone succeeding. Amanda truly cares about her students and also the class. I appreciated how well she taught the material; it was very easy to understand. At any point if you struggle or can't find your mistake on an assignment, go to office hours!

Amanda is so wonderful and full of energy even at 7:30 AM. If you have the chance definitely switch into her section. I hated math in high school but I actually felt like I understood it bc she explained it so well. She absolutely cares about her students success and I truly loved taking her class.

Seriously nice, and really focused on making learning more manageable for everyone. I learn really slow, and had previously failed the course with a different teacher, but I communicated my needs for a more personable environment, and she went above and beyond. Seriously, I should have bought her an Edible Arrangements for helping me pass the class

analysis.name: Amy Reibman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Reibman is a very nice professor. She may seem intimidating, but she cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Her homework can be tedious, but if you go to office hours, she will walk you through the problems. The exam averages are roughly in the 80's, and she usually targets them to be 75. Def recommend taking her classes.
Great command of the material. Exams weren't difficult at all if you understand the material. Best 302 Professor.

Lectures are average, lecture notes are very clear and nice to study from. Exams are fair in terms of content, but a big time crunch. Although I've mentioned some cons for Reibman, this is by far the professor you want for 301. She seems to care very much about students success and will accommodate new ideas/learning methods students suggest.

Overall very good, caring professor. Lectures could sometimes be a little scatterbrained/boring, but they felt like she actually cared about the content. Her homeworks were challenging, but interesting and actually fun to work on for the most part. Exams were very fair, high quality lecture notes posted online, etc. best 301 prof imo

Exams were HARD. They were long and each question was challenging. Lectures were fine, but having lecture late in the day was not ideal, especially since she speaks in monotone most of the time. Not a bad professor, but  there are better options out there.

analysis.name: Andrea Kasinski
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved this class. The so-called “disrespect” was really Dr. Kasinski asking persistent talkers to quiet down so others could hear. When they didn't, she raised her voice and asked late students to use the back doors. I respect her for protecting those there to learn. If you truly want to learn cell biology, take this class.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking this course with Dr. Kasinski! She made the content interesting and easy to understand in lectures. Homework was challenging, but the three attempts were helpful. Exams were similar to past exams and accurately reflected what was covered in class and the notes she releases after class.

Amazing professor. Lecture content is clear and engaging, tests are easy and match the practice exams, and homework can be slightly challenging. For other reviews saying she is “disrespectful”: she got frustrated at the class after several instances of people talking over her up to 5 minutes into the lecture, which I think is reasonable.

She has help sessions every week and most of her exams are similar to practice exams. Homework has 3 attempts with 2 weeks dropped. Same for participation points, which is basically 100 points for attending class. She walks the class through processes to help with difficult concepts. Favourite bio class so far.

Makes a very complex curriculum extremely easy to learn, great lectures, and overall just a very easygoing and articulate professor. There's barely any homework but it's still great practice for exams, and exams are pretty easy especially with the practice exams she posts. Really easy class but still very interesting.

analysis.name: Amanda Bies
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was a great professor and really cares about what she teaches. She wants you to do well and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. The text book is not really needed in my experience.
She's caring and passionate about what she's doing and has tone of experience
Lecture pretty much everyday but having the slides open would be useful. Also going to class helps with learning the material.

analysis.name: Amit Varma
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My favorite professor ever. He was very clear during lectures and provided amazing notes. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but was very helpful to go in person.

Hes one of my favorite professors. Explains everything really well and does good examples. Cares about his students' success too! I had an early class with him so its hard to stay awake but its worth it! DONT SKIP!!

Professor Varma made me love learning again! I seriously wish every graduate level professor taught as clearly as him. Hard to beat his course content for Structural Stability; it's very well developed, as he's taught this course for a number of years. He does take a while to grade assignments, but he grades fairly. One of Purdue's best professors.
Excellent Professor. Explains everything in great detail. Don't sleep in his class. Very helpful and very intelligent. Always comes prepared, great examples, I highly recommend.
Awesome professor and all around great guy. He's really good at explaining difficult concepts and makes you want to come to class!

analysis.name: Amanda Veile
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For a 3 credit class this was the easiest thing ever. Her lectures are very monotone and not the most engaging, but it was easy to zone out or do her homework during it and then get the attendance credit. There are no tests or quizzes, only online homework due every week. The labs were very interesting, and the whole class honestly felt fake.

This is probably the easiest class you can ever take in college. It is genuinely impossible to get below a 98 unless you just skip every class. No tests, exams, assignments are graded by participation, and on the homework you can answer as many questions as you want until you have a 100.

If you need to a UC science credit, I highly recommend you to take her ANTH 204. It's a free A. She gives out study guides before exams, and those study guides are basically the exam. Also, it doesn't even matter if you fail those exams because she provides tons of extra credit opportunities. I can feel her passion in her lecture. Amazing professor

overall not a bad class. lecture attendance is mandatory but the lectures tell you everything you need to know. most of the class is just inquisitives and the lab recitation. only thing that irks me is the way she says potentially.

She is so amazing!!! ANTH 204 was recommended to me because it is a science that is easy to follow, and it is great if you just need the credit. Dr. Veile makes it easy to get her students to achieve.

analysis.name: Amy David
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The assignment's grading rubric is extrme not clear, and the assignment always happened before lecture (you have to finish before learn the knowledge for this homework). When combine these two things, you will find even an AI will did better than you in the assignment. Also the professor will never tell why you lost your points in the feedback.

What a confusing class. Prof David was helpful during office hours but the entire semester-long project and lectures were super confusing from start to finish. She made video projects due the day after we get back from spring break. Communication was awful and grading system is weird, with everything pass-fail. Not hard, but strange - just be aware

There is no textbook. Lectures have very little content. Not much more than the powerpoint slides and sometimes the exercises/quizzes require you to know more than what the lectures teach. What was most annoying to me was the inconsistency in grading. Short answer questions would be scored 0% or 100%, even though the question was subjective

The farther away from her the better. I didn't learn anything from her. She only reads PowerPoint and does not give grades or standard answers until the end of the term. The mentor is fine. She didn't even check out our group's initial mistakes until our mentor checked them out before the final presentation.  she's ridiculous.

Do not take this class. I have been confused the whole semester. Her lectures are dry and not helpful. Very little content and wants you to do a project with Pepsico where she hands out  Word and Excel documents to do it all by yourself basically. Avoid this class. If this is required for your major, good luck.

analysis.name: Amy Marconnet
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Marconnet is a talented heat transfer professor. Her homeworks are long and at times tedious, but typically written in a way that leads students to the answers. Lectures are well-organized, although I would prefer if she leaned less on written-out equations presented rapid-fire and instead derived them herself at a more reasonable pace.

The class has an unreasonable amount of work and has some of the most challenging homework assignments I've experienced between both my undergraduate and graduate studies. The exams are similar to ME31500, but slightly less challenging. While most classes acknowledge that projects take time and effort, ME50500 doesn't slow down to accommodate.

Professor is a nice person, giving great lectures. There is no doubt you could learn real heat transfer, as well as some essential tools that engineers need. Unavoidably this is a difficult course, hws were super time-assuming, but exams were fair at most of the time. But no worry, she is generous but reasonable at final curve.

Prof. Marconnet seems to be pretty new to teaching. Tries to cram too much material into each lecture/week. Homework assignments were incredibly long. Added a group project to an already overbooked course. Responded well to emails, but was unforgiving and not understanding to conflicts and technical difficulties. Class was unnecessarily difficult.

She is a great lecturer, but tries to fit way too much material into an extremely short amount of time. The homeworks take forever. You will have no life if you take this class, burn out, and count yourself lucky to not have your wife divorce you by the end of it. Oh, there's a final project too. You *just* have to invent something completely new.

analysis.name: Steve Amireault
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Excellent speaker and keeps me engaged. Class is interesting, he doesn't give a crazy amount of work outside of class, exams are fair, and his slides are easy to read.
Cannot understand what he says in lecture and slides are a bit confusing but it's an easy class with online tests.

Honestly, if you turn something bigger than a lab report in expect at least a month before you get your grade back. And his lectures are just him reading his slideshow that he posts online. And expect to do multiple papers, and projects all at the same time at the end of the class, and him not being helpful when you reach out to him out of class.

Steve-O cant get things graded on time-- at all. It took this dude over a month to grade a 2-3 page outline of our research paper when he expected to read and grade everyones 10-12 page final drafts the 5 days of finals week. He needs to learn how to structure this class correctly or he will honestly lose his job. Nice guy though.

His time management is really rough. Lectures never get through what is planned and we were typically behind because of rambling. Grading of papers typically took very long and feedback for it wasnt very helpful. He cares honestly but the class didnt run very smoothly and can be stressful.

analysis.name: Arezoo Ardekani
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The worst teacher in my graduate school.  Poor planning for classes and worst teaching experience. Dont take this course and read from the textbook. Just a waste of time.

At first,  she was really hard to understand because of her accent and the way she talked was kind of monotone. However, stick to going to the lectures and you'll know that they are really helpful and clear. She is also willing to help if she notices that you put in the work. Great teacher.
I loved her for thermodynamics. She clearly answers your questions and knows a lot about the subject. I definitely passed and actually learned  because of her.
Lacks basics of good teaching: preparation, passion and knowledge. Any takeaway from this course required self-study on my own.

Probably one of the best professor's you will get in the ME department. Loved her lectures. She brings notes to class for everyone - so even if you show up with just a pen you would be perfectly fine. Much better than some of the other professor who teach THERMO here.

analysis.name: Arshak Petrosyan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Late to class, runs over time, but truly a passionate teacher. You can see him getting excited about class problems that he can probably solve in his sleep. He will run through how to solve things step-by-step. Minor accent, but shouldn't be an issue.
Undoubtedly the best math professor I've had so far at Purdue. He teaches you what you need to know, and he does it well.
Avoid him if you can. He's a professor who dated a PhD student
Good lectures. Not really accessible outside of office hours. Standard real analysis content is covered... but demoralizing exams

Great professor, his online lectures during covid were great. First exam was easily manageable, but exam 2 and the final were very challenging. Homeworks are useful for learning, and gave his time to make review videos before exams (which were open notes but hard). Last two chapters of the class were very confusing and could be explained better.

analysis.name: Arkady Plotnitsky
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: (engl 223) He is a very difficult professor, he assigns a lot of books. When it's time for lecture attendance isn't for a grade, and he barley talks about the books we read; he tends to ramble. He does grades based on two essays and a mid term and he harshly grades them. All essays are 7 pages long, but sometimes he will say it's too short.

He's a good person, but not a good professor. He spends the whole class rambling about things that have nothing to do with what we are learning and never asks questions. He doesn't give a rubric for papers so you have no idea what you are doing but then grades them hard.

I took 223 and all I learned was from reading the books. He tends to ramble lecture and repeat himself. Only ever studied one viewpoint of a topic and he rarely asks questions. Offers extra credit all-or-nothing for attendance. 3 grades. Very interesting man but this causes a lot of namedropping. I'd look elsewhere unless you need his course.

[eng223]
most important thing is that he teaches how to THINK DEEPLY ABOUT THE WORLD, not the books. yes he rambles- about the THEMES in the text (which is what he cares about in papers! trust i got A+ on all). he's lenient if you ask for an extension, and graded fairly even when he disagreed with my viewpoint. the class is difficult but he's not.
Literary theory is more often than not based in philosophy...duh. Plotnitsky knows his stuff and is able to teach it in a way that makes it fun to learn.

analysis.name: Donu Arapura
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: NEVER EVER EVER EVER walk out of his class in the middle of a lecture. He has a very particular set of skills, skills that he has acquired over a very long career. Skills that make people leaving his class a nightmare. If you leave his class, it will be the end of you.

Do not take if you want to learn. He'd avoid answering questions (very small class) and would be annoyed when he did answer them. He ended early every day, and when a student would stay "after" (class time not yet officially over) to ask something, he'd act like he was being forced to help. Gave very little notice, if any, for important things.

Would face the board, writing most of class, would have to speak out because he'd never see your hand raised. Never put any exams or in class quizzes in the gradebook. Seemed very nonchalant and didn't really care. Way too many proofs too

Professor Arapura simply did not care about this class. He once wrote a theorem by saying "the new method is the same as the old method". If you want an interesting math class, do not take a class with Arapura. If you want an easy A, I would consider it.

Professor is very smart and has mastery over a seemingly broad range of mathematics. Lectures and course content can be dull but that's expected from a second course in linear algebra anyway. He's fun to talk to. Sometimes I wish he challenged us more.

analysis.name: Dorsey Armstrong
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I love Professor Armstrong! One of the best teachers I've had at Purdue. She cares about her students and really wants them to do well. She's always available to help with class assignments. As long as you put forth your best effort in the readings and writing, you should be fine. She's a very cool, down to earth person. Take a class with her!

Her lectures and overall demeanor was always entertaining. She is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. While there are occasional pop quizzes, as long as you stay on pace with the schedule, you will be fine. There is a lot of reading, especially towards the later half of the semester but it's an English class.

She makes English literature engaging. Exams and quizzes are super easy if you do the reading and show up to lecture. Her essay assignments are extremely clear with what is wanted, and she gives you prompts or you can use your own. This is without a doubt the best non-STEM professor I've ever had at Purdue!

Dorsey is possibly the best prof I've had at Purdue! Wish I could have her again but I'm graduating! She makes the information interesting and is obviously an expert in her field! She grades fairly and gives you multiple opportunities to do extra credit papers and there is extra credit on her exams. Take a class with her if you can!!!

Armstong is one of my two favorite professors from my undergrad career. She's a GEM, both as a person and as a professor. She commands respect, but is kinda motherly towards her students. You will learn a lot about medieval lit and history in her class, you'll become an enthusiastic nerd like her, and you'll love it.

analysis.name: Arun Prakash
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Course is a lot of work, but taught well. Average week is: lectures, homework, quiz AND MATLAB project. There are 4 "Live Quizzes" during the semester that are essentially mini tests. I felt this class took time away from others to do well. Prof is always available and gives 2 attempts on hwks and quizzes. Review MATLAB and Lin Alg prior to course.

He is a good professor, but his teaching style really made things too complicated. Despite investing twice as much time as other courses into completing various assignments and quizzes, you may find that your grades do not reflect the effort you have put in. I think AAE 558 (FE Methods Aerospace Structures) is more helpful than this course.

This prof gives SO much work it is never ending. Definitely a class you have to stay engaged with or it's a steep hill to catch back up. Felt like grading was on a pendulum between very lenient and very strict. His lectures weren't the best but not terrible. Definitely needed the curve at the end. He is very accessible outside of class too.

Dr. Prakash takes a very rigorous approach to Statics. He explains in depth and assigns the most difficult problems. You really learn the material (and if not, you won't do too well...). He is exceptionally helpful, not only offering regular office hours but also in the semester I took the class, regular review sessions. Inspiring, great prof!

Prakash is approachable, kind, and explains topics thoroughly. If you have trouble deriving expressions symbolically, you may struggle in lectures, but he does lots of examples. HW is graded on effort, exams are hard but have lots of partial credit, and extra credit for attending lectures. Overall, would recommend Prakash.

analysis.name: Ariel De La Fuente
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He only graded us out of 4 tests, but the tests were based almost 90% of his lecture. Only two questions in total were not covered in lecture.   He covers the readings during the lecture very well. His lectures are long and boring, but you can usually use him as an audio book and focus on something else.
Very interesting class. I really enjoyed the professor too. A few midterms and quizzes as well as an in person essay at the end. Highly recommend

Lectures can be a bit bland, it's just material but he does a good job of explaining content. I'd highly recommend going to lecture, there are no videos posted and it's easier than reading the slides from home. Read the textbook too!! I found that to be a great resource.
Absolutely despised this class. Do not take it if you have a choice! By far the worst class I have ver been in, professor sucks and so does the structure of the class

This professor changed the topic of the class throughout the semester. He eliminated about 1/3 of the books he listed as required by the end of the semester. The majority of the class ended up being about Argentina (I like Argentina but that was not how it was advertised). His lectures ramble and his quizzes & exams were unpredictable (mildly put).

analysis.name: Tyler Atanasov
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I have Tyler for 505 (not an option in the class menu yet). Many of the slideshows are poorly made, his lectures are dull and confusing, HW is using Excel and completing it helps with nothing else in the class let alone exams, and the only practice for exams are giant FRQ packets not even made for exam studying use, despite the exams being all MC.

Rating him now, as I found out that I have MGMT505 with him next semester. I had him in his first semester teaching. All I have to say is that I am really hoping he's learned from that first go-around, because if it's anything like 305, 505 is going to be harder than I thought.

Tyler is what the average person thinks accountants are like. That works for some, but for most it's pretty difficult to adjust to. He is a new prof, so my expectations weren't high, but between the lectures being optional and unhelpful, and ~90% of the class grade being dependent on a handful of exams, there's a reason why I barely squeaked out.

Incoherent lectures made going to class a total waste of time. Not sure why this one bothered to become an accounting professor. He has no interest anything other than imposing what little power he has over students.
Worst “professor” I ever had.  Has zero professional experience and a tepid understanding of accounting at best.  Unclear lectures and does not respond to student emails.

analysis.name: Dwight Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Useless feedback, irrelevant rubrics, meaningless lectures, and bizarre emails are some things present in his classes. I almost failed until I explained how work should be graded, but then I was lectured for pointing something out and made fun of. He's only valuable for his research as the teaching is horrid. Don't take him even if there's no chce
One of the best professors I have had in my academic career. Is very passionate and knowledgeable, but also one of the most humble people I know. It was a pleasure having him as my professor.
Unstructured, unorganised, and weird.
This class was very stimulating. It was one of the best classes I have ever taken.
What a great course!  He is extremely nice and helpful.

analysis.name: David Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is an exciting lecture, engaging, and make his class interesting. He proctored class discussions that were actually interesting. The class consisted a two essay exams but there were not difficult even without reading the text books. My favorite aspect is that even after a year and a half, he still remembers my name when I passed him in a hallway

Take good notes during lectures (which is easy because they're so interesting) and you'll basically know how to most of the classwork without studying. Definitely the best class I've ever taken at Purdue, and it's mostly thanks to Professor Atkinson and his incredible charisma. He makes you wish power hours were longer so you can keep listening.

Dr. Atkinson is God's gift to Purdue. His lectures were really interesting and he is clearly passionate about the subject. There are few grades but if you do the reading and put in a good amount of effort you'll be fine. One of the best classes I've ever taken at Purdue!

Amazing teacher. Three homework assignments throughout the class that aren't too time-consuming. Three tests require you to write about concepts covered in class which are also not too challenging if you go to class and pay attention. He is also hilarious and very caring. His lectures are worth going to.

I took HIST 152 as part of Purdue's Early Start program. I could not have asked for a better first class and professor at Purdue.
In high school, history was "This happened... then this..." and so on. Dr. Atkinson emphasized the significance. WHY was this important? His lectures were very entertaining and legible. He is just a genuine, humble guy.

analysis.name: Attila Hertelendy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: There was a long list of assigned readings that were not needed. Majority of the people in my course agreed that the text book was not useful nor needed. The professor was very lenient with due dates, meaning you could submit an assignment beyond the date it was due. Others in my course agreed that some major assignments lacked clear guidelines.

I wish he taught all of the courses for Purdue's online MPH program. Great professor and great feedback. He clearly cares about the student actually learning, and I really appreciate this. His expectations are clearly laid out and he is fairly accessible (although he does travel). I HIGHLY recommend taking any course taught by Prof. Hertelendy.

This professor is just not kind to his students. He states he is flexible then refuses to work with students regarding travel plans and trips. Learn how to connect and impact your students positively rather than be controlling and rude.

analysis.name: Annabelle Atkin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Atkin was great! I loved the class and the way it was structured! Very organized as you knew what you were going into each week. She was a pretty easy grader as long as you did what you were asked. Textbook was needed for about half the class for weekly comp. quizzes. She incorporates many outside videos that make it more interesting, as well.

While I felt this class was educational, there was way too much homework. Reading assignments were essential if you wanted to do well on the quiz and blog post due at 10 pm Sunday and they would be like 30 pages long on top of another reading assignment or videos/podcasts. Attendance basically mandatory . She is nice but it felt like a power trip.

She was very hard grading things that were irrelevant to the course material, such as citations being perfect. She also made attendance points worth 5 instead of the regular 1 surrounding holidays when you might have to miss class, which dropped my grade and I felt like that was unfair. She also gives a lot of homework. Not a fan.

analysis.name: Mikhail Atallah
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Probably the best professor I've ever had. He does an excellent job of explaining material in a manner that is easy to understand. He keeps lectures interesting, enjoyable, and educational.

Gets side tracked very easily and expects students to go beyond anything learned in lecture to complete the homeworks.  He may be a very intelligent man but he needs to work on the fact that he's teaching undergrads without any phd's! try to avoid this guy.

Atallah's exams and homeworks were extremely difficult, but he was extremely helpful outside of class. He was willing to re-explain topics in different ways, and even scheduled additional office hours for anyone who asked. That alone displayed an interest in teaching and a concern that students learn the material that most professors cannot match

Despite what other students have said about this course, the professor obviously cares about the course material and is ready to teach it to those who want to learn it. He uses a very hands-on approach, and expects participation, which makes sense in a class like Algorithms. As a non-major, the course gave me a new respect for Computer Science.

Makes everything very difficult to understand.  Thinks everything is 'trivial.'  To him, it is - he wrote a book.  He teaches you a bag of tricks instead of how to solve and learn algorithms.  Does not know how to explain.  Homeworks are extremely hard and graded unfairly.  Tries to make you come up with a new algorithm based on what you learn.

analysis.name: Athula Kulatunga
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: At first, I had a little difficult time understanding Prof. Kulatunga, since his accent was a little different.  After a few weeks, I got use to it and started to really like him and enjoy his class.  I feel that I really learned a lot in class and it was always enjoyable doing some of the things we talk about in lab.
This is definately a class that you can sleep in and still get an A.  This is almost as easy as ECET 107.  If you don't get an A in this class you need to quit ECET and go to Liberal Arts.
Just a tough grader that is very strict. Extremely smart guy but expects things that we just flat our never learned before.
so umm ya whats going on in class.  Good luck to all 157 students with this one.
