We had presentations for 355 which he told us the day before the actual details of what he wanted us to do. then he mocked the people who got picked to present and kept making condescending comments about how they didn't do enough research even though he told us what to do the day before...
do not take class, you are being taught by ai and not the professor, might as well take it for credit at ivy tech

John Burr is tough but if you want to go into consulting, he WILL prepare you well. He is a hard grader on presentations, and he can spot BS a mile away. (The course material makes it impossible to BS the group work/projects.) 4/5 Cases were in November, which was too much for one month, but he said he'll fix next sem. Not a blow-off class for sure

Definitely a hard professor, but he's only looking out for you since consulting is a hard industry. 4 straight weeks of cases are unfortunate, but in consulting you are constantly working so I can understand why he does this. He tries his best to help his students. This class is only rewarding if you put in the work.

analysis.name: Sridhar Budhi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Budhi is a kind, helpful, and approachable CHM 11510 professor. He chats with students before class and around campus. Though some struggle with his accent, he posts lecture slides and recordings. Tests reflect class concepts, and he avoids spoonfeeding answers. Despite teaching >400 students, he tries to get to know each one. Great guy, 10/10!

Genuinely an amazing, respectful person with a heart for his students. One of the best teachers I've ever had in my life. I felt welcomed into university knowing I could walk down the steps after lecture, say hello, and shake his hand. Although I don't have him anymore, I'm going to try to meet him for faculty lunches.Course wasn't too hard either.

He cares a lot for your success and proves it by the amount of time he pours into his students. He offers study sessions prior to each exam and is willing to communicate with his student directly instead of going through a TA. His exams are pretty easy and he provides plenty of study material to help you do well.

Had Dr. Budhi for ochem. Fantastic guy who really cares about his students success. When he saw that our test average fell he felt as if he failed us as a teacher. While he does have an accent, its not hard too adjust to it. He posts every lecture online and office hours are incredibly accessible and helpful.

Best professor ever. He truly cares about his students and values their time. He makes himself available outside of class. In class he cracks random jokes, then awkwardly points it out when no one laughs. When you laugh, he keeps awkwardly going and stretching it, he kills me. He also rounded my grade up by 3%. Such a kind and genuine man overall!

analysis.name: Greg Buzzard
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is very approachable as a person. All of his lectures are very well organized. He always starts conceptual, and then moves on to examples that are useful in the online homework and in exams. He tries to interact in lecture, and if a student gives a wrong answer, he looks at it from their perspective and explains where they were right and wrong.
Teaches concepts well. Very helpful. Makes it fun sometimes

Wonderful professor. Always smiles and makes the lectures fun, keeps the class alive. I wasn't enrolled just wanted to sit in his class and he was super supportive of this, his attitude really helped motivate me.

I really enjoyed Buzzard as a professor. He shows great examples and gives time for you to try things on your own. I found it very helpful to go to office hours since the class was hard but he does a great job of explaining things, especially during 1 on 1. Funny guy and really enjoyed
Very smooth and well organized course. Went through the basics of probability and random variables clearly.

analysis.name: Darcy Bullock
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class isn't horrible, just a ton of pointless work, and most of it is just busy work that barely relates to the topic. He is very enthusiastic about the topic which is great but he doesnt know how to give a reasonable homework or even exam preparation.

Possibly the most enthusiastic professor I've ever had. Homeworks take a very long time but only one is due per week. Exams are open-note and based very heavily on homework with plenty opportunity for bonus points. Lectures tend to get sidetracked or sometimes feel irrelevant, but overall fairly average for CoE. Lots of work but not hard to pass.

He's nice enough and knows the material he's teaching, but is not considerate of your time at all. Homeworks, while not necessarily difficult, take hours, and many homework questions and quizzes require a separate time commitment outside of just answering the questions (physically going somewhere on the edge of campus just to take a picture)

The exams and HW he gave were very reasonable. Learning primarily occurred outside the classroom through reading the textbook, but going to class is still a good experience because he provides some nice real world examples.

Great professor.
The homework problem sets are long and can take up to several hours.
The work isn't at all hard but it is time consuming.
The exams are fair and based on the homework.
Attendance isn't required but I would strongly recommend it if you want to do well.

analysis.name: Christian Butzke
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great easy class, great prof, definitely choose in person section. Textbook required. Take with friends!

This class is not necessarily an easy A. You have to memorize a lot of inane details for the tests. First half of semester is kind of fun. Second half is insanely boring. Take HW to do during lecture.

This professor is pretty much the king of wine. He knows every detail of every piece of wine information possible, and will teach you ALL OF IT. The class wasn't as easy as it seems as you have to know over 700 slides of information per exam. Exams are 80% of your overall grade, along with a wine visit and class serving teams. (20%) Overall not bad

Took class fall semester of senior year. It was during Covid so the class was virtual for me which kind of stunk but made it crazy easy. You can find answers to any assignment online and even if you do terrible on your wine video you still get full credit. Lectures are interesting just super long. Cheers

Good professor, known mostly for his wine appreciation class. Concentrated too much on the history and background of different wine regions, a lot of theory. Did not teach how to identify flavours or aromas during actual tasting. Still a great course, helpful in real life.

analysis.name: Buster Dunsmore
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 147 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He makes IU jokes, what more do you need?

A well respected and humorous professor who does his best to keep endless black and white PowerPoint slides of code interesting. Lectures will never be a good way to learn how to code but Buster does his best. (recommend reading the textbook since it's hard to focus in class)

I enjoyed doing the work, however, at some point the amount of work was unreasonable. Like another user mentioned, we had a project, homework assignment, and team project all while studying for an exam. The exams were on paper and it was heavily graded. Not to mention this course lecture heavy, although the prof is very humorous during lectures.

This professor reads straight from PowerPoint, focusing on random concepts like sentinel variables instead of practical coding skills. Vocareum, the coding platform, provides vague feedback, making it tough to learn. TAs lack expertise, and overall, the course feels more frustrating than helpful. Test out if possible.

The semester I was in unbelievably hard for no reason. We were employing CS182 and CS251 concepts into our code and expected you to be a god at coding. The group project was worse because one of my teammates dropped the course and one of my other teammates was useless. Then that teammate threw my peer review. I coded 75% of final project btw.

analysis.name: Kelly Blanchard
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 276 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: If Blanchard ran for president I would vote for her. In all seriousness, I feel like she was one of my best teachers at Purdue. Even though my grade wasn't an A i did learn a heck of a lot more than I thought I would and it actually brought me to eventually minor in Econ. She's a very helpful teacher and very knowledgable as well.

Dr. Blanchard is one of the best professors I have had during my time at Purdue. She really cares about what she teaches, and she wants every student to succeed. Super approachable and will answer any questions you have. Great at slowing down and using lots of examples to help students understand the material. If you can take her class, do it!!!

GOD BLESS KELLY BLANCHARD. She writes her notes out during lecture, which makes it super easy to follow along. I think I opened my textbook once the entire semester, and that was just so I didn't feel like I wasted my money. Tests are kind of difficult, but there are tons of past exams available to study from (she keeps her them very similar).

Amazing Professor. Lectures were very helpful and she is very good and making the information easy to understand. Up to 12 extra credit points can be awarded for hotseats and there's one homework per week. The only downside is that her exams are very difficult average is usually a 70. She gives old exams to review as well. Always offers help.

Best teacher I have had so far. She gives really good lectures and is easy to listen to. Got a 98% in the class. BTW it is almost an identical course to AP microeconomics, which I took in high school. Plenty of extra credit opportunities so do those too. Tests are easy if you understand the material. Didn't even buy textbook, can find info online.

analysis.name: Heejung Byun
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Byun is an amazing professor who truly cares about his subject and his students. The course work is light but relevant and effective. I would highly reccomend this class to everyone.
Half of your grade comes with the final and a project due during finals week which sucks. Overall energetic guy and class is not too time consuming

I switched into a 7:30 section to have Professor Byun. Never regretted it. He is super kind, very knowledgeable, and overall one of my favorite business professors. The class consisted mainly of a few short writings (1 paragraph max), some case study analyses, a midterm, final project, and final exam. AI is encouraged on the final project. 10/10!

Lectures were very interesting and easy to follow-he really cares about what we are learning about. There are case studies, so there is a decent amount of reading, but the cases are easy to be interested in & he's not harsh on grading. His midterm was difficult imo, but the average wasn't bad. Final project is not difficult, AI is encouraged!

Taking this class with Professor Byun was one of the most fun experiences I had at Purdue! The class was very interesting to be in and he was very well prepared for each class. Highly recommend this class and this professor. Wish there are more professor's like him out there who are out to be a good person and inspirational teacher!

analysis.name: Byunghoo Jung
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The problem with this class isnt the professor, its the way its designed. its a trap induced to fail students. i dont blame jung for making this class hard but his attitude towards us at the end was horrible. he didnt respond to emails when we asked for our grades/grade boundaries (finals) and i still dont know my final exam score so thats that

Prof. Jung's lectures were engaging and he explained the most conceptually difficult parts of 2k2 well. His dad jokes were some of the best moments of an otherwise tough class. The exams this semester were brutal, but not written by him, and he did his best to prepare us for them.

Professor Jung's lectures were incredibly hard to follow and were not very well organized in terms of content. The textbook for the class was way more helpful his lectures. No homeworks in the class, just 2 exams and 2 design project submissions. All learning happened by reading textbook, searching for things online, or talking with classmates.

This is actually rating for ECE20002. Lectures more complicated than needs to be, much material not covered on HW & exam; can also move fast at times and was still behind schedule. HW more complex than what was on exam, but TAs will help. Exams were mostly fair, but little in class practice or review. Overall, ok; just review material periodically.

ECE 201 is a hard course but Jung makes the best of it. He puts a lot of work into his lectures and tries to ensure that students understand the concepts. Homeworks are useless for exam practice (much more time-intensive than actual exam problems). Focus on doing past exams and you will do well.

analysis.name: Alan Bunning
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed Professor Bunnings lectures even though they were always the latest one of my days. He is knowledgeable in his field of specialty. He explain how the mechanisms behind both hardware and software. He is an easier grader than his colleague. If you are new to coding, SIs are helpful for exams from my experience.
Great lecturer but you have to keep with the work to be successful.

Bunning always had good informative lectures that were easy to follow and take notes. However, the CS159 course is terribly designed which is not Bunning's fault. Group labs were terrible as one person ended up doing most of the work and the grading on the your code being efficient rather than working was not cool. If the code works its works.

Does iClicker questions at the beginning of lecture for attendance. Answering them at all is sufficient. Don't talk too loudly during lecture or he'll call you out. Don't share homework code with one another, they catch it easily. His notes cover almost all the material; I'd say the book is redundant. Exams are tough - know your concepts and terms.

Professor Bunning was fantastic at explaining the C language. His way of teaching made learning more complex topics easier to grasp. While his lectures aren't the most engaging in the world, they are very informative and critical if you want to do well in this class. Overall, this course is overly hated and isn't too bad in reality.

analysis.name: Byung-Cheol Min
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took 315, and it was amazing! Prof Min demonstrated coding in class and explained it line by line, which was very helpful. Although the textbook was outdated, he provided updated materials as lecture notes. I wish CIT had more professors like him because he genuinely cares about the course. He has quickly become one of my favorite professors!

Min is an awesome professor. The slides are very high quality, he demonstrates respect for his students, and he is very helpful if you need it. The class can be challenging at times, but he is very helpful. Also shoutout to his TAs, they are very helpful as well. Plus he is a chill guy too.
You need to read many papers, but the professor will recommend it. There is a lot of homework but it is really helpful for your research.

I took Software Design and Development for Robotics Class taught by Dr. Min. Simply, Dr. Min is a great professor. He really cares that his students gain knowledge and not just pass the class. He understands his student's needs and makes sure to make labs and class as convenient for us as possible!

Byung Cheol Min is very hypocritical. He acts very nice and caring, but in truth, all he cares about is whether you can produce paper for him. Whenever you seek advice from him, he tries to tell you things that will benefit himself. He'd tell you to relax for your thesis defense and then you will give you a hard time during the defense. Stay away!

analysis.name: Cornelius Bynum
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bynum is so funny and so great. Attendance is not mandatory, but that is the only way to do well on the exams because those exams require information you can only get from lecture. Exams are three essays throughout the semester about the textbook and lectures, and those are the only grades in the gradebook. Just go to class and you'll pass.

Honestly the worst professor and the worst class I have ever taken at Purdue. All three of the exams (the only grades in the class) are based off reading the textbook and other assigned books. He doesn't believe in study guides, but he will let you bring in a list of what you think mine be short answer topics, but knowing the info doesn't even help

Professor Bynum did a really good job at teaching this course. I would not describe myself as a person who is good at history, but the way he explained the material just made so much sense. While your grade is only determined by three essays, as long as you engage with the assigned reading and attend class, it isn't too hard to do well.

Worst professor I have ever had. Often times goes on tangents about random things that have nothing to do about the class topic. Heard from some people to not take this professor, and to drop the class, wishing I did. I leave this class every lecture wishing I had never taken the class. Very poorly run class, grades are based upon 3 essays.

Professor Bynum is easy going but enjoys preaching his own political viewpoints rather than just teaching us history. Attendance is not mandatory and his lectures are irrelevant because only material from the readings are on the exams. If you want a class that you can completely blow off then this is the class for you.

analysis.name: Vetria Byrd
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Probably the worst class I've ever taken. The entirety of the course had 0 organization. Syllabus changed constantly. Multiple times she came to class asking us about a reading prompt she forgot to even assign us. This professor took an easy A class and made it impossible to follow. Lectures were also mandatory but had no relation to the labs.

Dr. Byrd teaches a masterclass in disorganization and poor communication. Right from the beginning of the semester Dr. Byrd and her TA excel at making things as difficult as possible for the student, making them go out of there way to find out whats happening. She treats the class as if its Junior High. She does the clap thing for silence like ????

The Byrd is an absolute terrible teacher. Gives quizzes based of dozens of pages of reading, and only has a single question from that reading on the quiz. She never talks about the quiz again. She will sometimes not even mention an assignment, let alone give us instructions about it. It really seems like she doesn't care about the students.

The worst teacher I've ever had. I was excited for this class because it has to do with my major, but it feels like she just throws a bunch of stuff at us with no clear direction. She doesn't actually teach, but gives us a bunch of videos to watch instead. I'm gaining nothing important out of the dozens of assignments we're given each week. Useless

The most unorganized professor. Assigns a lot of work with unclear deadlines and barely any instructions. Does not use lab time correctly. Does not teach any relevant information during lecture, makes students teach everything to themselves through readings and videos. We have finished the 5th week of classes and we don't know how to make anything.

analysis.name: Charles Catalano
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is the first time ive really cared about an english/lit class in a long time. Charlie is inspirational and really cares about his students not only in his class, but going forward. Hes the type that will say hi if he sees you 2 years after you had him. Im bad at public speech, but hes a forgiving grader and gave me Bs on all my speeches.

It is clear how much Charlie not only loves his job, but loves other people. He showed genuine care for his students and clearly wanted everyone to succeed. My favorite moment was the line of students after our last lecture lining up to give him a hug, or just thank him. If you have to take SCLA102, take it with Charlie.
Charlie is an incredible professor with genuine passion not just for what he teaches but for life in general

Professor Charlie has been the most passionate professor I have had at Purdue so far. It is clear that he cares about his work and the impact on students. He does a great job of bringing the real world into the classroom for deeper learning.

Charlie was an incredible professor. Within the first week he learned all of the student's names and truly cared about our growth through the semester. All of the assignments had appropriate deadlines and were easy to complete. He helps students through speech anxiety and wants to inspire everyone daily. Books were cheap, and many extra options.

analysis.name: Charles Campbell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have taken multiple classes with him, and from those I have figured out, he is a very unorganized professor. Moving around exams last minute, giving the wrong amount of time for test, not grading the homework, along with changing the syllabus or not providing one to follow. He has made many students drop out and retake under another professor.

He gives little to no feedback and when he does he phrases things extremely vaguely and to the point where you have no clue what he's actually saying. A lot of reading is needed. his organization skills are bad to say the least we had a full schedule planned only lasted 4 weeks. There are pop quizzes throughout the class that are you can't makeup.

For a written communication course, it was harder than it had to be. Late graded assignments, not following the syllabus schedule, vague assignment descriptions, vague and unclear communication, one-size-fits-all teaching style, condescending attitude, and a few, if any, applicable constructive feedback on essays and written assignments.

Initially a very tough professor but he gets nicer over time. Makes you really work for your grade on the essays but is easy with other assignments. He's very intimidating but not a bad teacher. He provided a lot of guidance for the final essay but the first one was basically us going in blind. Not impossible to get a good grade though.

Not as bad as described, but expect late grading and unclear information on your grade, and surprise mini-quizzes that will contribute to a significant portion of said grade. If you actually do the reading and come to class on time, you'll do fine. Stress on the time bit since the quizzes are usually done in the first 2 minutes.

analysis.name: Cecelia Harper
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. I took this as an elective and would recommend to any student. She teaches very real-world scenarios that everyone should know about law, crime, and contracts, very applicable. She makes lectures fun, engaging, and is understanding about absences. A real lawyer, very good to learn from.

Professor Harper was very nice and helped to wake you up bright and early. The class was fun, with many good team projects and some quizzes. She was a bit of a strict grader though, and the workload was a little much for a 1 credit class though.

Professor Harper's MGMT 254 is the most fun I have had in a class in college. The class is difficult, but Harper is always ready to help in anyway possible. She understands that there are things that go on outside of her classroom and is very respectful of her students time. The work is heavy but you are given a lot of time to complete it.

This class was very disorganized when I took it. She also would not respond to my emails on multiple occasions. Homework assignments are also disorganized, filled with spelling and grammatical errors as well as asking questions not covered in the book or slides, but are usually pretty easy. I had 3 midterms and a comprehensive final.

One-credit course with quizzes based on the textbook and more. Independent studying was required, as not all quiz material was reviewed in class. Really strict grader, and way too much work for one-credit.

analysis.name: Cary Troy
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Best professor in the online graduate course options for civil engineers. He is helpful and willing to work with you. Awesome professor.

Cary is an absolutely phenomenal professor. Lectures are very good and thorough. Coourse's content is interesting. The one thing I don't like is the hw grading. I believe TAs graded them and sometimes they take off points even when the qs don't ask. The project is very time consuming so be prepared for that, and pick a good partner.

Professor Troy is funny and kind. His lectures are fast, so make sure to pay attention. His Friday lectures are just time to work on the homework and he provides the answers: you still get graded on work. His exams are fair, and he is just a really good professor. I actually cared about learning the material and found it interesting because of him.

Hilarious/amazing educator. Chill environment, connects and engages every student. Class Slack is super helpful. I never felt the need to read the textbook & you don't need it for hw. Go to office hours and Fri class (working hour) to finish the HW. Records all lectures. 3 exams + the final. HIGHLY recommend Troy; favorite professor I've ever had.

This is hands down the best class I have taken at Purdue. Troy's dedication to his student's learning is clear, and he makes class fun and interactive. He gave out fill-in-the-blank packets every lecture which were extremely helpful. The Friday class was a mandatory office hour to work on your homework with other students. The exams were very fair!

analysis.name: Cezanne Elias
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Most of the class is spent with a mentor who is an undergrad student who has taken HDFS 100. Dr. Elias was nice and an easy grader. The whole class is projects. There are 3, which are all very easy, and have multiple parts. She gave a week by week schedule which was followed exactly so you always know what to expect when you go in.
I learned so much in this class. It is very participation oriented but it is not difficult at all. I would absolutely take it again!

This class was very easy, however Professor Elias was often disorganized or unclear. Her study guides are not helpful and exams can be tough, but going to class and reading the book is really all you need to do well on the exams. Sometimes lectures are a bit boring, but she is overall friendly and there to help. Not a great professor, not terrible.

Sexuality and Family Life with Dr. Elias is a great class. It is a mix of traditional lectures and guest speakers. The tests are very straight forward. A lot of the information is just expanding on high school health class. Dr. Elias truly cares about all of her students and makes adjustments in the course every semester based on feedback.
Super nice professor and really fair grader. Attendance really matters in this class but I plan to take her classes again in the future.

analysis.name: Cecilia Tenorio
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class that I took isn't listed as an option (SPAN485), but MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR AT PURDUE. So sweet, caring, accommodating, clear grading criteria, FUNNY, extra credit opportunities. Gives lots of anecdotes from her country (Argentina) that gives me real world application to using the language. Also this was a cooking class! We made tamales!

This professor is great, she is very caring and is very helpful with all her students! There is quite a bit of group work (having to meet once a week) but it's nothing too overwhelming. The content is pretty easy and interesting to learn!

Tenorio is now my favorite Purdue professor. She is so incredibly knowledge in her field and keeps her lectures so incredibly interesting. Her feedback is so detailed and personalized that you really learn from your mistakes. Take this class! Take any class with her. She is like the abuela youve always wanted to teach you a spanish course.
She is a straight savage (in a good way). I have learned very much from her and am very glad to have taken her class.
Exceptional teacher, really knows her stuff.  Makes class really interesting and fun.

analysis.name: Cecilia Mun
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is the worst professor at Purdue. Don't ever take her class. She interrupts students giving their presentations if they forget even the smallest thing. She doesn't give examples of the citations that she wants. She is really critical. I should have known this class was bad when she made us read our syllabus out loud on the first day.

One of the worst people ever. Does this annoying where she puts in the wrong grade and then doesn't change it until weeks later. Doesn't create a comfortable environment but expects us to discuss sensitive topics like sexual relations. Shuts down students and forces them to conform to her ideals about feminism, patriarchy, and society.
Overall confusing and frustrating to work with. I think she meant well but she generally didn't listen.

analysis.name: Suman Chakraborty
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Chakraborty is an excellent instructor who genuinely cares about student learning. He frequently connects concepts to real-world engineering problems. He is also very approachable and always willing to help. Exams are tough.

He's a terrific lecturer and is very nice and approachable outside of class. However, the way he ran this course was awful. Homework and exam grades were often not given for months after the deadline, and the midterms for this class were genuinely impossible. He also assigned a literature review due 2 days before the final. I hope he improves.

Had Suman for an online course. He was terrible. Consistently late with posting assignments, content and grades.  Never provided feedback to the class for our final projects and assignments. It felt like he was rushed at the end of the course to make assignments up then he dumped a ton of work on us without much notice. Worst online course ever.
Nice guy, but the course is a huge drag and lectures are way too long and boring. straightforward A/A- though, just a ton of busy work.

Professor was borderline sadistic at times. Would make extremely difficult exams and smile as he walked through the aisle seeing students struggle. Assignments would be graded weeks after being turned in. Purdue prop specialization is so disorganized.

analysis.name: Christina Li
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Li is so good. I loved her and I'm hoping she teaches other classes because she made me really excited to come to lecture. She's very personable and easy to watch. Highly recommend to anyone who struggles with coming to lecture because you'll want to come with her lecturing.

My number 1 thing with her: she writes out all of her notes. This is insanely helpful. Thermodynamics, kinetics, and equilibrium are all math heavy concepts, and her drawing everything out makes it so much more digestible. Very few profs seem to be putting in the effort to write out all of their notes. Her speaking abilities are strong.

Loved her as my professor. You could tell that she was engaged with the course content by the way she lectured and answered questions. I found it super helpful that she projected hand written notes as she lectured, rather than just teaching from premade slides. Her lecturing pace was perfect.
Handwritten notes rather than reading off slides, and she is generally friendly.
Li was a great teacher! She explained things really well and gave mathematical examples as well as demonstrations. She teaches at a really good pace also, and she's super sweet and funny!

analysis.name: Celeste Furtner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

The labs have mandatory attendance but were the same as the prelab. Lecture videos were posted same day with the course participation being due at midnight that night.

Marta was very caring and overall the class was extremely helpful, however I find it much more beneficial to watch the lecture recordings instead of attending lecture because she moves really fast and if you have a Mac it is more complicating. There's a group project that lasts the whole semester and it is sort of confusing but graded very easy.

Marta is a great professor. Her lectures aren't mandatory, and you can always watch videos from class online. Labs are mandatory, but there is usually homework so it's a good time to get that done. A semester long group project takes up a big part of your grade, but it's nothing bad. Tests are long but as long as you did the HW you're fine.

Marta is a great professor. She is very clear in explaining things and wants her students to do genuinely well in her classes. The course was structured really well. It sucks that this is the last semester she is teaching this course. Overall, if you get her as a professor, you'll do well. Just make sure to do the work and ask questions.

analysis.name: William Crossley
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, the professor was excellent in the lectures and put in some effort to be available outside of class. Grading was usually fair and the regrade policy was generous. Flexibility in assessment and project due dates was extremely helpful and greatly appreciated. I would definitely take another course taught by this professor.

Interesting course, teaches non trivial topics very well as he puts in a lot of effort in the course. Only complaint is that feedback for homework takes a long time to get, dont expect to get feedback before the semester ends. But it's doable if you pay attention and try, just a lot of work. Recommend the course.

Content was good but course organization was very poor.

-Homework releases were routinely delayed or bugged, sometimes without notification

-Homework grading and feedback was terrible. Took about 2 months for the second homework to be graded, right before the last homework was due. No chance to make improvements because of lack of feedback.
He has all of his bad reviews removed from RateMyProf. Tells you everything you need to know

Took as an online student. Interesting material and fair grading. I'm not a big fan of his lecture style since it seems like so much of it is watching him fill in the notes. I'd rather have him focus more on the concepts/interesting tidbits/motivations since the math itself for MDO is pretty easy to follow on your own in general. Overall good class

analysis.name: William Crum
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I came into this class with zero coding experience and now I absolutely love it. Crum is a great lecturer and the homework assignments help one get a better understanding of the material, although they are very time consuming. At first the class seems impossible but if you put the time in to learn, youll do great. Oh and DO NOT CHEAT IN THIS COURSE

Horrible teacher. Exams had me on all fours especially with the MCQ as there was always the option for “none of the above”. Lectures are extremely content heavy and Crum teaches until the last second and CRAMS all the content he can. He has the lecture notes packet but never follows it so it gets confusing. Get another teacher🙏🏻🙏🏻

The class is very reliant on knowing advanced geometry always focusing more on geometry than actual coding. There are "course standards" that make everyone follow the same absurdly exact formatting. Miss a comment on one variable? Didn't like the name of a variable? Points off. Very very harsh graders (the TA's). DEFINITELY NOT an intro course.

I have never felt so defeated by a class before. I did not have much previous experience with coding and this is supposed to be an intro class. The labs and homework are difficult but they are worth basically nothing. The exams are very difficult and not like the assignments. They are also the majority of the points. Not easy to help. SI is a g.

Crum's full understanding of the C language is very apparent when he lectures. He explains concepts clearly and well. I loved him as a professor - I would have taken any other class that he taught. The exams and labs in this class are difficult, but Crum and the TA's are willing to help. Overall - Crum is a great guy and great professor.

analysis.name: Melba Crawford
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Crawford is a decent lecturer, though she tends to use language and terminology that surpasses what we have learned or what we should know for the exams. She has some really neat experiences in the field, and overall seems like a cool person. She does provide lots of good resources for the exam, but TAs will be your best resource when studying.

She is an ok professor, I think that I say ok because the content was pretty advanced and you have to play close attention and read the textbook to understand what is going on. She definitely knows what she is talking about, but with no prior experience in photogrammetry, it was difficult to keep up, but that might just be the course.

Mumbles sometimes, sit near the front.
Consistent with surprise quizzes
Really hard midterm not a whole bunch of study material either

Lectures are tough to understand. In class quizzes at least once a week. Exam was difficult as well, 40+ MCQ's and 7 Written Questions. Labs can be long and take significant time to complete. Labs also require software that cannot be installed on personal computer, requiring you to use software in computer lab.

Random in-class quizzes at least once a week. The exam consisted of around 40 multiple choices (worth 50% of exam) and around 3-4 pages of free response questions (worth 50% of the exam). Both parts of the exam were confusing. Not hard to get at least a C since the class is pre-curved, but the course is tedious.

analysis.name: Steven Crain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Crain was a great professor. He had a clear grading rubric for every assignment, taught us everything we needed to know to get an A, and gave good feedback. Everything was clear cut in his class. His lectures aren't boring and he keeps everything upbeat. He treated everyone respectfully even if they didn't do the same. Overall great guy.

Dr. Crain is the best lecturer I've had at Purdue and the best teacher I've ever had! He is very caring and genuinely cares about his students learning the materials properly. He offers a ton of extra credit and grades very fair. He provides lots of feedback on his grading so it is easy to learn and improve. I wish I could have him for every class.

Dr. Crain was wonderful. I was very nervous about taking this course, but he made it very easy and clear. He truly does care about his students doing well. He will work with you and your schedule, even asking students their availabilities before assigning presentation dates. If you're taking COM 217, please choose Dr. Crain if you can!

Dr. Crain is one of the best professors I have ever had at Purdue. He is provides great feedback on all speeches and has a genuine care for his students. He can be a tough grader at times, but gives plenty of opportunity for extra credit at the end of the semester!

Dr. Crain is great! As a com major in a science presentation class, I thought that I would struggle, but it is very similar to COM 114 (I'm pretty sure they use the same textbook too).Though the textbook was necessary for the quizzes, they don't won't ruin your overall grade. I averaged 3/5 on most of them and still ended the class with an A.

analysis.name: Brett Creech
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor takes a while to post the grades for projects. Other than that, he is a good professor and is not too strict with the grading of presentations and papers.
I took the 4-week summer course for COM217, and although it was condensed, the course didn't feel overwhelming. The professor gave good feedback and is not a harsh grader.

Cared a lot about the students and made public speaking approachable. Lectures were very fun and down-to-earth; made it worth getting up at 7:30 for them. Offered office hours on weekends before each presentation week and graded very generously for speeches. Got everyone donuts for the last class.

analysis.name: Craig Voll

He actually makes me want to go to class, and enjoy it! Craig is very caring and supportive of all of his students. He strives to have a personal relationship with everyone. If you have a chance to take a class with him, DO IT!!

Professor Voll is an incredible professor. All of his students adore him and he is very personable to everyone. For example, before every class he plays music and says hello to every student who walks through the door, he usually knows them by name. He always has a smile on his face. I will be taking another class with him, he is amazing.
WE ARE DONE LIKE YESTERDAY'S DINNER
Professor Voll is a wonderful person.  This is my favorite class.  He gives out candy, and the class is actually entertaining.  Please take his class.
Amazing professor and person. He enjoys what he does and it shows!

analysis.name: Laszlo Csonka
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This man needs to retire. He is obviously knowledgeable about the subject but he is just an awful teacher. He reads off the powerpoint slides word for word in a slow, almost inaudible monotone voice so there was no point in even attending class. The powerpoints werent even good, so you often have to consult the textbook for clear answers.

Dr. Csonka is one of the worst biology professors as his teaching style is horrible as he only wrote on the chalk board with an outline given to the class. His tests are mostly application and he does class discussions that he randomly selects students to answer the questions. Students only knew 40% of their grade before it was on their transcript.

Dr. Csonka is simply a very bad instructor. I was disappointed to find that Biol 438 was co-taught by him and Dr. Applegate. Applegate was great, and it was a shame Csonka brought him down. Csonka doesn't really teach, he just very quietly reads off powerpoint slides. People stopped coming to his lectures because there was no point.

He's a really nice guy, especially if you're in one of his smaller (i.e. not the core bio) classes. He was very helpful with lab experiments in the class I took with him, and even did the experiments himself in case we messed ours up so we could see how it was supposed to turn out.

Dr. Csonka is an amazing professor. He is incredibly intelligent and cares for his students. He does have a thick accent which may be hard to hear through but it is able to be deciphered. Overall love him and would take his class again.

analysis.name: Gabor Csathy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He has a cool accent. Sometimes a little hard to follow but is usually pretty clear. Always checks clicker answers to make sure the majority of the lecture understands the topic and if the class is split or not getting it he goes into more detail. Seems to really enjoy the topic and teaching. All around a nice and good professor

With Gabor, the course really wasn't to difficult, essentially his lectures are from the textbook and he uses a lot of examples from the textbook and the practice exam. His exams are straightforward and relatively easy. Put in the effort and you should be able to get a good grade no problem.

He was just an OK prof.  All he did was read the lecture notes and besides the clicker points, there was no reason to go to class.   He was not the worst prof I have had here but definity not the best either.

Prof. Csathy's lectures can be dry to some, but he tries his best during demos and explanations. Physics is hard, but if you learn the lectures/ ppts., you'll be ok. Expect the following: 2 midterms (averages were 50% & 55%!!) and a final, weekly lab reports, weekly online homeworks, and iClicker participation. 7 - 8% curve at the end of the sem

He's one great guy!  His Romanian accent is awesome and just that alone sometimes made me want to come to class.  Explains things very well and you can fully understand him.  Some may just find the subject hard.  Although I said attendance was mandatory, it isn't, it's just that you have clicker questions you and get some points for being there.

analysis.name: Tara Cuthbertson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Cuthbertson is a very caring prof. She encourages group discussions a lot which can be good or bad depending on whether or not you're a person that likes that. I found her grading pretty fair. If you think she's a harsh grader she still gives a) tons and tons of feedback and b) allowed me to resubmit essays I did really poorly on.

Dr. Cuthbertson is probably the best professor I have ever had. She is caring, passionate, and very knowledgeable. Though she is a tough grader, she is more than willing to help her students and provides the means for them to succeed. Get ready to have a fun, philosophical, and mostly stress-free class!

Dr. Cuthbertson's class was a highlight of my week. She was always ready to make class fun but also a place where we could learn and ask questions. The class is based entirely around readings done outside of class, but they usually aren't super long. Participation is important and she'll try to get everyone to talk, even if it's only one thing.

The professor is very caring and understanding. She gives opportunities for extra credits and have a very fun personality. Participation matters a lot, you should contribute to class discussion semi-frequently to do well in class. I love that the books she requires for class is accessible, cheap, and have rich literary history and importance.

Other reviews said she was a strict grader, but she really was not. I got nothing lower than an 86 and I am a terrible writer. She cares lots about her job and even more about her students. She can talk for a while, but she encourages class participation, and it is nothing boring. She was probably by best professor this past semester.

analysis.name: Thomas Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AAE 340 used a terribly difficult class. Prof Cunningham is improving it so that the material is learned thoroughly without making the content impossible. Lectures are very dry and not worth much, but homework is engaging and kind of fun. Exams are a time crunch but are graded generously. It is obvious that Prof Cunningham cares about his students.

Was not a good professor. Acts like he is caring and kind but will penalize grad students for working. Homeworks were 5+ hours and he didnt explain in lectures. He is a printing guy playing space. Run. RUN. RUN!!!

Cunningham is the GOAT. I had him for 203, 251, and now 450. Each time he made learning the material fun and, by extension, easy. He has unc status. He's that guy who is always looking out for you, but will challenge you in ways that make you grow. 10/10 professor and 10/10 person.

(shoutout Talaria and the entire Despicable Me franchise)

This is the quintessential Cunningham course. Very clear lecture style, first half of the course is a breath coverage of the spacecraft subsystems which can be a little dry if you are already familiar with them. Second half of the course is much more interesting coverage with failure analysis and operations procedure. Also very joyful person!!

Thomas Cunningham is who you want all your AAE professors to be like. Great notes, charming guy, and he makes a somewhat boring class (203) pretty interesting. Occasionally gives hints for HW and gives great tips for exams.

analysis.name: Alejandro Cuza
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Abysmal. I came into this class a fluent native speaker with C1 profiency and left feeling like I'd never encountered Spanish in my life. To this day I do not speak a lick of Spanish and find most episodes of Dora impossible to follow. DO NOT TAKE.
Heavy material but lighter grading, Meaning if you come prepared for tests you will do better than expected. Excellent class for improving Spanish.
Great professor, very funny as well. Participation does matter, easy A

analysis.name: Xingshan Cui
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Simply a lovely professor with care and consideration for his students as to what they need to know to succeed. His provision of relevant examples are incredibly important for understanding and while my grade may not reflect that, it is without a doubt that he is an excellent professor especially for showing critical 3-D shapes in relation to math.

Cui was a great professor overall. His lectures are very clear and help you understand the topics. He also goes over many of the upcoming homework problems which makes doing the homework easy to understand. Has great test review lectures. I knew many calc 3 students who had other lecturers that went to Cui's lectures instead.

Prof Cui has an accent and not the best handwriting, which I didn't really have a problem understanding after the first couple days, but if that is typically a problem for you, maybe consider a different lecturer. Overall, seemed like a nice guy, lectures were good, but exams were stressful.

His lectures follow Chenflix pretty closely and he keeps them lighthearted. Sometimes he stumbles on his words but he has good pacing in his lectures. You will be there for the full fifty minutes, he never ends early and sometimes fills with proofs not needed for the class.

Professor Cui did a very awesome job teaching calculus III. He goes over most of the proofs (though not required to know) which will help you understand where the equations come from. Lecture notes are always posted on brightspace after class.

analysis.name: Jason Cutter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cutters Aviation Systems class might just be the easiest youll take outside Nolans AT10000 class. Theres one group presentation at the end of the course, and the tests are basically the study guides with answer choices. I had the 0730 slot and even though I sometimes fell asleep, I still had an A. If I can pass, you can too.

Pretty easy intro class with a couple of papers to write. Took less than 10hrs total over the whole semester to do, and 1/2 of the grade is just by following instruction on stuff like formatting and having a title page. Attendance is by QR codes at end of each class and they count towards the grade.

Dr. Cutter is very clear about the way he grades things and emphasizes the importance of communication. Gives good insight on the industry. The assignments consist of multiple papers that won't burden you as long as you start early.

Easy class. Grade is basically determined by turning in research papers and there are lots of extra credit points given out if you still somehow don't have an A. Speakers are interesting, but definitely a filler class for you to have more credits. Mandatory attendance.
Was transparent about grading criteria. Emphasizes communicating problems early and paying attention to instructions, which was not bad if you just put in the time. Overall easy class and professor.

analysis.name: Mark Cushman

He is always super nice and checks in with students during lecture with clicker questions to see if "learning is occurring" and gives extra credit for these. His question on exams and quizzes were always easier and better understood than his counterparts questions. This man is my favorite.

This professor made me hate Purdue and pharmacy. Pray you never are required to speak to him. Im a quality student and I achieved my desired grade but this professor is terrible in understanding and speaking to students
daddy Cush is so cool I love him and he taught me a lot about organic things I am smart so I got an a+ but I can't say the same for others. -cc

Dr. Cushman cares about students' comprehension.  He gave quizzes before and after class (not for credit) to check on whether "learning was occurring."  He is also excited when you answer his questions correctly, pumping his fist and going "Yes!"

analysis.name: Cynthia Koh-Knox

review_highlights.comment: PHPR 202 would be great if there were fewer people telling us what is important and what is not.  There is seemingly little communication b/t lecturers, so one cannot answer all the questions.

I think she thought that using guest lecturers would give us more view points, but it was not helpful.  Also, study everything for her exam, even if she gives you "focus  points", because she may not stick to them.
Class is so easy, only one project and a few lecture reflections. Make sure to go for attendance. Easiest A of college for sure.
Eclectic individual with some great stories to share.
Could careless about nursing students. Uses a lot of guest lectures so she doesn't have to do anything. Not helpful. Did not stick to study guide.

analysis.name: Cynthia Fortner

review_highlights.comment: She's worthless when it comes to explaining homework assignments, essays, or any other important part of any college english course. Picks favorites and ridicules her other classes during class, including names of students she dislikes which I found annoying and unprofessional. Shouldn't be teaching.

I am an English major, and she made me consider changing majors because of her negative and unconstructive "feedback". I always made great grades, and was in AP English in high school, but she dropped my grade from a B to an F the 2nd to last class of the semester and told me to drop out-because I missed ONE class due to an emergency. HORRIBLE.

An amazing professor!  We did not have a "certain" textbook, but we did have to purchase three novels.  She can adapt the material covered in class with issues or subject matter, but maybe influential to the class.  She gives very positive feedback, extremley helpful, but she tends to get sidetracked.

She is the best professor I have ever had at Purdue. Sometimes she is not clear with her saying but it makes sense afterall.  she is very helpful and knows how to make an intersting class for her students.
She is so passionate!  It's infectious.  It's obvious she loves her work and that makes it easy for me to show up and do the work.  She likes student discussions and lets us create our own projects.

analysis.name: Justyna Czader
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: SCLA101 is an easy course, with very doable work and an easy grade, but Dr. Czader herself is not a good professor. She can't teach well, and can't relate to her students or understand them at all, and leaves your outcome from the course as really lackluster and bare minimal. Easy course, but theres definitely better profs out there for SCLA101.

Listen, I respect a strict teacher. But she was beyond that, she would make fun of of other classes and would start conflict for stupid reasons. She has a problem admitting she is wrong at times, and her English could be better. Very monotone and seems like she hates her job. If you get her as professor, at the very least switch professors.

Unpredictable mood, can be strict, can be playful. Seems unapproachable though appears to want students succeed. Can be intimidating and doesn't hesitate to indirectly call out faults in front of the class.

99% of the professors at Purdue enjoy their job or at the very least treat you as their own. Czader does neither. Consistently mocks or is rude to students who have made genuine mistakes (in some cases for no reason at all), Goes on tangents trying to make points about something that has nothing to do with the assigned reading, makes up rules.. etc

I was on her good side, idk if this is due to my reading the syllabus/instructions or some other reason. She is fairly strict on grading with somewhat arbitrary rubrics, but if you put in effort and read the material, you can succeed. Once we got further into the semester, it became apparent she did care, but hard to tell with her behavior.

analysis.name: Daniel Suter
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: lectures are very dry and monotonous.Exams are impossible to get a good grade on if you do not have a photographic memory. I would not recommend for people who are not Neurobiology majors.

Dr. Suter is the nicest guy! His class is moderately challenging. If you go to class, read the book, and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. Make sure to go over the study questions because he definitely uses those on tests. Just put in the time for the class, and you should be able to get a really good grade.
Very caring professor, lectures are content heavy but exams are very fair. A lot of studying but enjoyable content.

Great person he's super caring and accommodating, however class is very hard. No matter how much you study you won't do good unless you have a photographic memory. Picks very specific details for the exams and you have to know everything. Exams are extremely hard and there is next to nothing to make your grade better if you do bad on the exams.

Dr. Suter expects a lot out of his students, therefore his exams can be quite challenging due to them being so in depth and detailed. However, Dr. Suter himself is a great professor, super approachable, and loves to talk about tennis.

analysis.name: Taylor Daniels

Daniels the goat fr. Loves when students go to his office hours and takes genuine interest in students outside of class passions. Stay Juiced T Dan 😎🐐

Daniels might be in goat contention. Lectures are slow, but not boring. Very deliberate about all work. Explains everything in detail. Has great banter with students. Will send extra material to the entire class if even one person brings up a difficult topic. Won't let you leave office hours without understanding everything.
Awesome professor, cares about his students and their understanding of the material. Class is well paced and easy to follow, also holds lots of review sessions and office hours.
I had MA 266 with him. Amazing lectures. Super engaging. Even offered to write recommendations for students.

Not helpful. Lectures are rambling, disjointed, and poorly timed. Not a shining star of Purdue's Profs, teaching a BEGINNER class and exam averages are in the mid 60's and will blame anything but herself. Really just not a great teacher. Unclear about expectations, not helpful when asking for help, will not accept that her students failures are her fault. Don't expect going to classes to be helpful nor office hours, rely on the book only as she literally has no clue what is going on either. Does not fit in with the other professors at Purdue.

analysis.name: Michael Delgado
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Teaches straight out of the book. Homework is worth almost nothing and tests are open response, which make them excruciatingly hard. Had to beg for students to go to office hours, even offered a bonus point (just 1), still no one went. Horrible teacher

Each answer is a short response, so you really have to know your stuff. The curve only helps you so much but not enough to get the grade you want.
Never responds to emails and is poor teacher overall.  Avoid him at all costs
Worst professor I have had at Purdue. You have to do great on the exams, or else you won't pass. No personality at all. Good economist, AWFUL at teaching.

Avoid this professor, he doesn't know how to teach at all. Course projects are assigned by his subjects, if ask for a change of topic, he will say no without any listening. I never had any experience of faculty displaying so strong personal dislike toward students. He is the only one. Terrible teaching overall, and need more teaching experience.

analysis.name: Jonathan Delph
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: He was very difficult to work with and incredibly rude with every interaction, the homework's were long and strenuous (50-60 questions per), the lectures had a lot of information to ingest with very short time periods to do so. Overall, would not recommend to anybody.

I have never done so poorly in a course in my life up until now. The homework is weighted as if it were finals and being a day late on the homework is -25%. He gave a 60 mcq hw on the night of Thanksgiving and I was 2 days late to it, answered all questions correctly, and got a D-. Begged him for forgiveness because it dropped my grade by 2 letters

The lectures were crammed with way too much content in very little time. Felt like I was constantly behind on work. Jeffrey is a very caring professor and it is obvious that he wants his students to succeed. However, this class was a nightmare. Do not take if not required.

Dilger made this class memorable and he made it obvious he is passionate about teaching. I also recall this class requires some extroversion, as most lectures will require you to collaborate with a possibly random classmate.

Very passionate about what he does. Makes it a point to make sure everybody's thoughts are heard. Very open and caring, strives to keep an accepting classroom environment. Overall, a great guy and great professor. It is a privilege to get to be in Dr. Dilger's class.
Where do I start? I love this man. If you can take any class with him, just do it. I don't care what the class actually is, do it.

This professor is by far the absolute WORST professor I have EVER had at Purdue! I have emailed her 7 times over the course of the semester and HAVE NOT once received a reply from her. She is irresponsible and rude. I've emailed the TA twice this semester and he has NEVER emailed me back either. I just don't understand this lady.

This class was sooooooooo easy. I did all of the online assignments the first week of class and then did not have to worry about them again. The lectures are super boring.  I could just feel the life being drained from my body. You'll get an A if you do the work, but good luck staying awake.

Laura Downey has been the first Purdue professor to make me question whether or not choosing higher education was something beneficial to me. I have done nothing to question my intelligence whilst completing work that I have not been prepared for in any way, shape, or form. Technologically incapable, and the lectures were blunt. Seems unprepared.
Very unhelpful professor. Will not make any accommodations for anything, even if there is no reason not too. Mediocre lecturer, not too hard of a class, but very unsympathetic and stubborn.

analysis.name: Stephen Durbin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gets all material from the University of Maryland, even notes. He doesn't teach. You are assigned readings online. There is no textbook. You go to lecture and he asks you questions that you work in a group with. He doesn't give a clear answer to the questions. There is not enough time for labs and they are very difficult. He is very rude/ unhelpful

One of the worst professors that I have ever had at Purdue. Questions and examples done in class are never given a clear answer. There is not enough time on exams. The recitation is extremely difficult. Questions on exams and equations needed are never even hinted at in class.

He uses all of Maryland's material. I don't even think he looks at his slides before he comes to class. We are never given a straight answer, even when we do clicker questions. We spend the whole class going through one useless whiteboard problem that does not correlate to the exam material.

class was decent. TAs for labs and recitation are easy graders. make sure u know the material bc the tests are mostly just conceptual. challenge problems are sometimes interesting and sometimes just busywork depending on what u r interested in. don't take this course if u aren't all that interested in physics, especially with the challenge problems

Reverse classroom!! Tests are extremely concept heavy with little to no computation questions. Boilerexams help, but concepts should be studied as a supplement. The TAs were very easy graders, but the tests are from hell because of the low question count. Challenge problems are fun and labs are basically participation. Homework is difficult though.
